LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images Last week in the NFL was full of drama. The Cleveland Browns came back from down 17-0 to defeat the Houston Texans , while Kirk Cousins was victorious in his first game back with the Minnesota Vikings . The San Francisco 49ers and Dallas Cowboys put up 86 total points in Arlington, and the Cincinnati Bengals blew out Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers on "Sunday Night Football." This week there's more. Fernando Mendoza will make the first road start of his career against an aggressive Denver Broncos defense, the Detroit Lions will begin life without Aidan Hutchinson at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , and the Vikings will play the 49ers in Mexico City in what could go down as one of the best primetime matchups of the entire season. There are many, many massive spreads in the NFL this week! Which teams should you pick in Week 11, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 18 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Indianapolis Colts at Houston Texans (-12.5) (TNF) Dajani (Texans -12.5): I would typically lean toward a huge underdog like this in a divisional game, but two factors have me leaning the other way. One, Daniel Jones threw for just 108 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions last week against the Miami Dolphins . They were starting a quarterback that had never played in the NFL, yet only lost by two points. Jones has been terrible. He's turned the ball over an NFL-high 15 times and has the worst record in primetime by any quarterback since 1970 at 1-16. Additionally, the Texans allowed the Browns to come back from down 17-0 and win their meeting last week, which I imagine has this Texans team seeing red. C.J. Stroud and Co. are better than their 3-6 record indicates. They even beat the Jacksonville Jaguars earlier this season. I think the large number is justified. … Prediction: Texans 27, Colts 14 Dubin (Colts +12.5): I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. … Prediction: Texans 23, Colts 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions (-7) Dajani (Buccaneers +7): Jahmyr Gibbs leads the NFL in rushing yards this season with 1,000, while the Buccaneers allow the fewest rushing yards per game (79.2). The Bucs also lead the NFL in rushing offense and in takeaways with 21. With the Buccaneers coming off their bye week and the Lions coming off an international trip that cost them Aidan Hutchinson for the season, I'm leaning toward Tampa Bay with the points. The Bucs are 4-1 against the spread in their last five games, but keep an eye on the quarterback situation over the next 24 hours. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 21 Dubin (Lions -7): The Bucs likely playing this game without Baker Mayfield pushed me in this direction. Jalon Daniels is fine, but I don't expect the passing game to be able to do much here. The Bucs base the entire offense around the run anyway, but the Lions are actually pretty tough to run on. That could change without Aidan Hutchinson, obviously, but I don't think it will change enough for Tampa's offense to keep pace with what the Lions are likely to do. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 16 Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10) Dajani (Broncos -10): I don't think Fernando Mendoza wins his second career start in an environment like Mile High, but can he cover the double-digit spread? Denver has won just one game by double digits this season, back in Week 7 against the Arizona Cardinals . The Las Vegas Raiders, on the other hand, have covered in four straight divisional games for the first time since 2022. The Broncos are coming off their bye week and have scored at least 26 points in each of their last three games. Bo Nix has also thrown multiple touchdowns in back-to-back games. The Raiders are tied for the worst scoring defense in the NFL this year with 28.9 points allowed per game, so I think the Broncos could reach 30 points this week. That could make it tough for Mendoza to cover the spread. He's actually the first rookie quarterback to ever face both of the previous season's No. 1 seeds in his first two career starts. … Prediction: Broncos 30, Raiders 17 Dubin (Raiders +10): The Broncos have seven wins this year, and six of them are by one score. The only team they beat by more than seven points is the Cardinals. I reserve the right to change this pick if Brock Bowers is out and Fernando Mendoza just doesn't have anyone at all to throw the ball to, but otherwise the Broncos just don't seem like a team capable of blowing out an opponent that has actually played fairly well this year. … Prediction: Broncos 21, Raiders 17 Jacksonville Jaguars (-6) at New York Giants Dajani ( Giants +6): No one is debating that the Jaguars are not one of the best teams in the NFL, but they haven't exactly been tested recently. They blew out the hapless Colts, had no problem with Joe Fagnano 's Baltimore Ravens and then dropped 40 points on the one-win Tennessee Titans . The Giants aren't Super Bowl contenders, but this is easily the best team Jacksonville has played in over the past month. I'm not going to take the Giants to win this game straight up, but I am leaning toward the six points. The Giants have an underrated defense that currently ranks No. 5 in the NFL in yards allowed per game (305.7), and J.J. McCarthy has the fifth-most yards per attempt (8.8) since his Giants debut in Week 5. Both of these teams are 6-3 ATS this season. Give me the Giants with a back-door cover. … Prediction: Jaguars 23, Giants 18 Dubin (Jaguars -6): Unlike the Broncos, the Jaguars have blown out everybody. Five of their seven wins have come by 17 points or more, including each of their last three games. The Giants are probably better than the Colts, Ravens and Titans, but I don't see them hanging with this Jacksonville offense — not with the Jags getting their new defensive stalwarts on the field for the first time since the trade deadline. ( Jessie Bates III and Jordan Davis sat out last week because they had yet to have their bye and the Jags had already taken theirs.) … Prediction: Jaguars 31, Giants 20 Minnesota Vikings vs. San Francisco 49ers (-3) (SNF in Mexico City) Dajani (49ers -3): The 49ers are coming off a ridiculous 46-40 win over the Cowboys, where they recorded the most total yards in a road game in franchise history (584) and averaged a whopping 9.4 yards per play. Brock Purdy's offense had three touchdowns of 65+ yards! Christian McCaffrey actually became the first running back in NFL history to record two 65-yard receiving touchdowns in a game. Obviously, the Vikings' defense is MUCH better than the Cowboys', but something you should know is that this game is in Mexico City. And both teams have prepared for it differently . The stadium the 49ers and Vikings will play in on Sunday is over 7,000 feet above sea level. So, the 49ers traveled to the U.S. Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs this week, which is at an elevation of 6,621 feet , to prepare. The Vikings, on the other hand, apparently built an altitude chamber so players can get familiar with "thinner air" before Sunday, but otherwise are seemingly pulling a Los Angeles Rams and just showing up on site the day before the game. The 49ers dominated the Rams in Australia in Week 1, 27-7, and part of that was because their travel plans were so much better. The 49ers have won and covered in four straight International games. … Prediction: 49ers 26, Vikings 20 Dubin (49ers -3): In a battle of a great offense against a great defense, I am usually going to lean toward the offensive side unless there's a really compelling reason in favor of the defensive-minded team. Kirk Cousins' ability to elevate the Vikings' own offense almost provides that reason, but it's not quite enough for me to get there. This San Francisco offense is too much of a well-oiled machine for me to pick against the Niners — even in a matchup with a defensive coordinator as crazy and as good as Brian Flores. … Prediction: 49ers 23, Vikings 17 Cincinnati Bengals (-6.5) at Washington Commanders (MNF) Dajani (Bengals -6.5): Before you think this is some easy pick to make just because of how hot the Bengals are, know that Cincy is 0-2-1 in its past three games against the Washington Commanders , who just upset the Giants in New York last week. Jayden Daniels ' coming-out party as a rookie actually came against the Bengals. Still, it's hard to go against my Super Bowl pick and my MVP pick this season. The Bengals are 6-2 SU and 6-1-1 ATS in their last eight road games and have scored at least 30 points in three straight on the road. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Plus, how to watch, what to know and a prediction before the 'Thursday Night Football' matchup Getty Images In the Week 11 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Houston Texans play host to the division rival Indianapolis Colts . Houston enters this game coming off a dispiriting loss to the Cleveland Browns that dropped the Texans to just 3-6 on the season and dealt a significant blow to their playoff hopes. The Texans need to start stacking wins, and they need to do it right now if they want to make a run at a back-end postseason spot. The Colts, meanwhile, snapped a five-game losing streak with a close win over the Miami Dolphins last week. They didn't exactly light the world on fire, though, and have the look of a team that is just playing out the string after their series of trades ahead of the deadline. Will the Texans bounce back, or will the Colts make it two in a row? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Follow the game live here Where to watch Texans vs. Colts live Date: Thursday, Nov. 19 | Time: 8:15 p.m. ET Location: NRG Stadium (Houston) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Texans -12.5, O/U 44.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Colts have the ball The Texans defense has been one of the most disappointing units in the league this season. Houston ranks 20th in yards allowed, 18th in points allowed and 22nd in EPA per play, according to Tru Media. The Texans checked in first in yards, second in scoring and third in EPA per play a year ago, and were expected to again field one of the top defenses in the league this season after returning almost all of their key pieces. Instead, Houston has struggled to contain opposing passing attacks, repeatedly leaking on the back end despite putting pressure on quarterbacks at an above-average rate. Players like Kamari Lassiter have regressed significantly, while Reed Blankenship has been a bust as a free-agent signing. Luckily for the Texans, they are about to face one of the most inept passing offenses in the NFL . Daniel Jones has been entirely unable to drive the ball in intermediate and deep areas of the field since returning from his Achilles tear, and it has neutered the entire aerial attack. Jones has completed a career-low 59.6% of his passes at a career-low 5.6 yards per attempt, with just seven touchdowns against a league-high 12 interceptions. The Colts also traded away both Josh Downs and Keenan Allen last week, leaving them with Laquon Treadwell , Ashton Dulin , Anthony Gould and Deion Burks as their main wide receivers. There is not an imposing player in the bunch. The Texans should be able to shut down this passing offense with relative ease -- especially if they can get pressure on Jones, who can no longer evade the rush like he did last season. He's already been sacked more times than he was a year ago despite playing three fewer games. The Colts have turned the dial down on Jonathan Taylor 's workload in recent weeks, having him split snaps and carries with rookie Seth McGowan , including in the red zone. Taylor played 81.2% of the offensive snaps through the Colts' first six games, according to Pro-Football Reference, but is at just 66.5% of the snaps since then, with McGowan's usage ticking up. Taylor has also not been as effective this season (career-low 4.2 yards per carry) as in recent years, which isn't surprising given the total lack of a passing game and the Colts' offensive line issues. Those issues should persist on Thursday, with both of Indianapolis' starting tackles out for this game. It's fairly difficult to run on the Texans to begin with (4.0 yards per carry allowed), and it should be even more so with the Colts in their current state. When the Texans have the ball C.J. Stroud is playing the best ball of his career, including his rookie year. Stroud checks in sixth in the NFL in EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media, despite the fact that he's been working with an injured and rotating pass-catcher corps for much of the season. The Colts are an easy bunch to throw on, checking in 27th in the league in net yards per attempt allowed (which accounts for sack yardage), and they won't have Charvarius Ward in this game and may not have Sauce Gardner , either. Nico Collins should see favorable matchups on the outside and be able to feast all night long. The likes of Tank Dell and Xavier Hutchinson could get in the mix as well, though they tend to rotate more heavily in and out of the lineup and therefore see fewer targets than Collins. It's also quite easy to run on Indy, which has leaked 4.8 yards per carry on the season, 29th in the NFL. The Texans, though, have been entirely unable to run the ball, with neither David Montgomery (who is set to return from injury on Thursday night) nor Woody Marks (who is out with a concussion) able to establish anything resembling success on the ground. Montgomery was averaging a mere 2.7 yards per carry before his injury, and Marks has been at only 3.7 per carry in Monty's absence. This is likely to be a game where the Texans lean heavily on Stroud to establish a lead, then turn to the ground game to run the clock out, in what should be a relatively easy matchup given the state of the Colts' roster. So long as the Texans keep Stroud well protected early on, that strategy should be plenty successful, even if it doesn't necessarily result in a blowout win because the Texans themselves aren't that explosive of an offense. I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. away.headline: Dolphins First Week 11 Injury Report: Brewer Status Quo, Punter Problem, and More
away.blurb: The issue at wide receiver is that rookie Caleb Douglas joined the list of injured players at that position as he was limited with a shoulder injury. There was good news there, though, with Chris Bell back at practice (albeit on a limited basis) after both he and Jared Wayne missed the game against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Along with the five players who didn't practice, the Dolphins had five others who were limited. Besides Bell and Douglas, there was LS Tucker Addington again (shoulder), CB JuJu Brents (neck) and C Andrew Meyer (neck). The Bills also had five players sit out practice Wednesday, with guard O'Cyrus Torrence's absence related to a personal issue. Furthermore, three safeties were limited in practice, including recent acquisition Amani Hooker (knee) along with Damar Hamlin (toe) and Cole Bishop (shoulder). Dolphins First Week 11 Injury Report: Brewer Status Quo, Punter Problem, and More Skip to main content SI.COM Center Aaron Brewer missing another practice as he remains in the concussion protocol clearly was the biggest headline of the Miami Dolphins' first injury report for Week 11, but there are several other issues worth monitoring. The most glaring ones would be at wide receiver, where injuries continue to happen, and at punter. The situation with punter Bradley Pinion missing practice because a right groin injury maybe shouldn't have been easy to predict after the Dolphins signed punter Jack Browning to the practice squad earlier Wednesday. As a general rule, NFL teams don't have two punters or two kickers on the team (active roster and practice squad) unless there's an injury, so the Browning move should have been a sign. As we indicated earlier, Browning has appeared in five NFL games but none since the 2024 season and hasn't even punted in a preseason since then. Wayne was among the five players who didn't practice, a group that included safety Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder/groin) and cornerback Jaylin Simpson (knee). Trader has been battling injuries for a few weeks now and one wonders whether he'll need to be shut down at some point to allow him to get back to 100 percent. While it's early in the week, the best projection if Trader can't play against Buffalo would be for Zayne Anderson to get the start alongside rookie Michael Taaffe even if Kyle Louis has been getting regular snaps on defense since coming off IR. Louis has been used as a type of nickel linebacker as opposed to a true safety. Simpson is primarily a special teams contributor, and if Wayne can't play again, then it would mean another game for veteran Jalen Tolbert. In the event that both Brewer and Meyer wound up sidelined for the Buffalo game, then we'd be looking at Jarrett Kingston, who played center for two snaps against the Colts when Meyer briefly left the game. The focus for Buffalo should be in the secondary, which was missing Wednesday cornerbacks Dee Alford (concussion) and Christian Benford (groin). Published Nov 18, 2026 ALAIN POUPART Ala

picks.blurb: Saints vs. Bears: Staff Picks and Score Predictions for Sunday Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The New Orleans Saints (3-6) face another difficult challenge Sunday when they travel to Soldier Field to take on the Chicago Bears (7-2). Coming off a disappointing loss to the Carolina Panthers , the Saints continue to struggle with offensive consistency and finishing games under head coach Kellen Moore. Those problems could prove costly against a well-rounded Chicago team that boasts one of the NFL's most productive offenses and a top-10 defense. Can the Saints pull off an unlikely upset, or will their struggles continue against one of the NFC's top contenders? Here's how our staff predicts Sunday's matchup will unfold. Grant Chachere, Lead Writer: L 28-14 This is a game that doesn’t favor the Saints. The Bears are by far the best team the Saints have faced since the Detroit Lions , who beat New Orleans in overtime. They have one of the league’s best offenses , led by quarterback Caleb Williams , and one of the league's most balanced teams. Defensively, the Bears have a top-10 defense. Chicago boasts a top-10 defense, ranking eighth in scoring (20.4 PPG) and seventh in total defense (310.9 YPG). Their strength lies against the run, allowing 91.1 yards per game (seventh-fewest), while placing 15th against the pass (219.8 YPG). Crucially, the Bears lead the NFL in third-down defense (22.8% conversion rate allowed) and rank 12th in red-zone touchdown efficiency (53.8%). They maintain consistent pass pressure with 26 sacks (ninth) and seven interceptions (tied for 11th). Also, this will be the first cold-weather game for the Saints as the temperature will be in the 50s throughout the game. I don’t think the Saints will pull off the upset, but what I do know is that the Saints have played better on the road as both of their wins came on the road against the Baltimore Ravens and New York Giants . I do think its defense will do enough to make this game tight before Chicago pulls away near the end. Prediction : Bears 28 Saints 14 Doug Joubert, Publisher: L 32-21 This is a Saints team that seems to be searching, searching for an identity, a consistent offense, people on the same page. The New Orleans offense sputters and coughs more than my old 1969 VW Beetle. No matter what I would do to that little air-cooled engine, it never could quite get started, and when it did, it usually took a few minutes of driving before it would get going smoothly. Once it was warmed up, that little thing was a joy to drive. Unfortunately, it took a while to even get to that point. The Saints O reminds me of that Beetle. They can't seem to get going in the beginning. Once they get warmed up and going, they are fun to watch. Until then, it's almost torturous to be a part of. Eventually, I had to get rid of that little car. Keeping the valves aligned properly on that rapidly expanding air-cooled engine proved to be one of those "I'll be doing this forever" kind of projects, so I just gave up and moved on. The New Orleans offense is at that point, in my opinion. A squad that cannot consistently move the ball, stopping and starting itself with poor run blocking, or wide receivers and a quarterback who aren't on the same page, or play calling that comes across as vanilla as can be (think runs in the middle). Now, Brandon Staley's group is another story, another car if you will. They remind me of a Tesla. The Saints defense can really get going with the first acceleration, but fade at the end. A battery-powered Tesla is a lot like that. They can fly right out the gate and tear the street up, but don't expect that to last, as those batteries won't go 300-plus miles (no matter what they say) like a gas-power engine will, losing energy much sooner than their gas counterparts. This Saints defense has produced through the first three quarters, especially for the last few games. Although getting turnovers has been a notable absence for this group, it has played well, up until the final quarter. To wit, the Panthers' game. I say all that to say this: you cannot do any of what the offense and defense has been doing against a quality team. The Panthers, Browns, and Steelers were not quality teams. This Bears team is. It will take a complete game, start to finish, for this Saints team to have a chance to beat Chicago. The local boys haven't done that all year long. Prediction : Bears 32 Saints 21 Saints Mailbag Wednesdays, On SI Saints will answer your questions about what we see from our vantage point. To submit your thoughts or inquiries click here . away.headline: Is Jordyn Tyson playing today? Latest update on Saints WR vs. Bears
away.blurb: What's the word on Jordyn Tyson? The New Orleans Saints rookie wideout was limited at practice to start the week, which was concerning. He spent months recovering from a hamstring injury after another hamstring issue cost him most of his first NFL offseason. He's going to be under the microscope anytime his name appears on the injury report. At least this wasn't another hamstring. Tyson picked up a chest injury coming out of last week's game with the Carolina Panthers , in which he caught 11 receptions, which meant he was limited at practice for most of the week. But he practiced fully on Friday and has no game status listed for Sunday's kickoff with the Chicago Bears . Expect him to be full-go at Soldier Field. The Saints will need him. They've only scored five touchdowns across their last three games, with head coach Kellen Moore slipping into even more predictable opening scripts as the pressure builds on him to deliver. We know Tyson will get his targets, if last week's game was any indication (and you'd assume he plays even more snaps after doubling his reps from his first game to his second). The challenge seems to be managing three different receivers and a pass-catching tight end in Juwan Johnson. Whether it's Moore calling plays or Tyler Shough spreading the ball around, the Saints haven't done a good enough job keeping Johnson and veteran wideout Devaughn Vele involved in the offense since Tyson made his debut. To that end, they haven't even gotten Chris Olave going early; his first catch last week came late in the second quarter. It's great that Tyson is ready to play. But he won't turn the season around on his own. If the Saints don't have the coach and quarterback in place to take advantage of all of these weapons, they'll have to find someone who can. away.headline: New Orleans Saints injury report: Five ruled out; Tyson good to go
away.blurb: The Saints will be without five players Sunday at Soldier Field, and the list hits the offensive line and the secondary hardest. New Orleans ruled out center Erik McCoy (biceps), right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee), tackle Asim Richards (knee), cornerback Martin Emerson (concussion), and safety Justin Reid (personal matter). None of the five practiced at all this week, so none of these come as a surprise, and Reid’s personal matter is the technical term for him being released by the team. The offensive line losses stand out most. Three linemen are out, including McCoy and Fuaga, and that’s a lot of reshuffling up front against a Bears defense that sacked Baker Mayfield four times in its last game. The back end is banged up, too. With Emerson and Reid out, cornerback Decamerion Richardson (thigh) is questionable after being limited all week. Linebacker Pete Werner (hamstring) is also questionable, even though he didn’t practice once after leaving the Carolina game. Questionable after three missed practices usually leans toward sitting, so I wouldn’t count on Werner. Either way, Caleb Williams should see a thinner coverage group than usual. The Saints did get some good news. Rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson (chest) was upgraded to a full practice Friday after two limited days. Alvin Kamara practiced fully after a rest day Wednesday, and running back CJ Donaldson (shoulder) fully participated all week. All three carry no game designation. Linebacker Isaiah Stalbird missed Friday’s practice for a personal matter but also has no designation. The New Orleans Saints submitted their final injury report of the week on Thursday ahead of their Week 11 contest with the Chicago Bears. away.headline: Who's in, who's out for Bears-Saints: Will Kyler Gordon play?
away.source: USA TODAY Touchdown Wire on MSN
away.blurb: The Bears have two players with injury designations with cornerback Kyler Gordon (shoulder) being ruled out and wide receiver Zavion Thomas (ankle) being questionable heading into Week 9. The Bears offense will get a big boost with the return of running back Kyle Monangai on Sunday against the Saints. Monangai has missed the last five games with a turf toe injury suffered against the New York Jets back in Week 4. Monangai's absence has been felt in the run game, which was dominating through the first four weeks before being average with him sidelined. Cornerback Kyler Gordon suffered a shoulder injury during a Week 9 win over the Buccaneers, and there was optimism the bye week would provide an extra week of rest and wouldn't require him to miss time. Unfortunately, Gordon did not practice all week ahead of Sunday's game against the Saints, and he's officially been ruled out. This will be the sixth game Gordon has missed this season. Bears rookie receiver Zavion Thomas was a late addition to the injury report on Friday. He did not practice with an ankle injury, and he's officially questionable against the Saints. We'll see whether the injury is enough to impact him for Sunday's game or, with a short week coming up, Chicago opts to rest him before Thanksgiving. But he practiced fully on Friday and has no game status listed for Sunday's kickoff with the Chicago Bears . Expect him to be full-go at Soldier Field. The Saints will need him. They've only scored five touchdowns across their last three games, with head coach Kellen Moore slipping into even more predictable opening scripts as the pressure builds on him to deliver. We know Tyson will get his targets, if last week's game was any indication (and you'd assume he plays even more snaps after doubling his reps from his first game to his second). The challenge seems to be managing three different receivers and a pass-catching tight end in Juwan Johnson. Whether it's Moore calling plays or Tyler Shough spreading the ball around, the Saints haven't done a good enough job keeping Johnson and veteran wideout Devaughn Vele involved in the offense since Tyson made his debut. To that end, they haven't even gotten Chris Olave going early; his first catch last week came late in the second quarter. It's great that Tyson is ready to play. But he won't turn the season around on his own. If the Saints don't have the coach and quarterback in place to take advantage of all of these weapons, they'll have to find someone who can. Monangai has missed the last five games with a turf toe injury suffered against the New York Jets back in Week 4. Monangai's absence has been felt in the run game, which was dominating through the first four weeks before being average with him sidelined. home.headline: 7 Saints players DNP, others limited on first injury report vs. Bears
home.blurb: Sheesh. The New Orleans Saints (3-6) shared a lengthy injury report ahead of Sunday's game with the Chicago Bears (7-2), with seven players not participating and two other limited to start the week. They'll need all hands on deck for a chance at upsetting one of the hottest teams in the NFL. Let's hope they can get it done. And let's start with the good news. Rookie running back CJ Donaldson (shoulder) returned to full practice reps on Wednesday after missing several games between that shoulder injury and a stint in concussion protocol. We haven't seen him since the rookie exited Week 9's game in Paris against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Donaldson has been a productive rusher for New Orleans on limited snaps (averaging 4.8 yards per carry and a team-high 64.7% success rate), and he was just starting to earn a bigger role after initially getting on the field as a short-yardage specialist. He competes hard in pass protection, too. How snaps could be divided between him, Travis Etienne Jr., Alvin Kamara (more on him in a minute), and Audric Estime remains to be seen. What about those seven players who didn't practice? We expected Kamara (not injury related) would get his usual rest day, which has been a pattern since he suffered a Week 5 back injury. He turned 31 this summer and has worn a lot of tread off his tires so it makes sense to give him a lighter workload during the week, especially if he's going to have a reduced role on game days. Kamara was only on the field last Sunday for 16 snaps but he scored two touchdowns. Veteran safety Justin Reid (not injury related) did not practice on Wednesday due to a personal matter, and head coach Kellen Moore was noncommittal when asked if Reid was expected back on Thursday. Stay tuned. Backup right tackle Asim Richards (knee) and a couple of defensive starters who got nicked up against the Carolina Panthers -- cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. (concussion) and linebacker Pete Werner (hamstring) -- were held out of practice. Additionally, starting right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee) and center Erik McCoy (biceps) both did not practice, though Moore said "we'll see" if either of them can return to work later this week. Two other players were limited to start the week: rookie wide receiver Jordyn Tyson (chest), who you can read more about here ; and backup corner Decamerion Richardson (thigh). We'll be watching for updates on their status as the week continues. This article originally appeared on Saints Wire: 7 Saints players DNP, others limited on first injury report vs. Bears

The Titans have yet to play a full, complete game this year. Even their Week 6 victory over the Indianapolis Colts saw Tennessee trailing 13-0 at halftime. away.headline: Report: Titans pass rusher involved in severe vehicle incident before Week 11 showdown
away.source: Last Word On Sports on MSN
away.blurb: Reports emerged on Saturday afternoon that an injured Tennessee Titans pass rusher was involved in a serious vehicle accident. Initial reports indicated that Jaylen Harrell was involved in the accident and was hospitalized with injuries. However, later reporting that Harrell’s level of involvement escalated into potential assault. Report: Titans Pass Rusher Involved In Severe Vehicle Incident Before Week 11 Showdown Authorities are investigating the circumstances of the allegations against the Titans pass rusher involved in the accident, so nothing substantive can be said yet. This is the third serious incident involving a Titans player in recent months. Calvin Ridley allegedly committed assault in Nashville, and Jordan Elliott was released after attempting to retrieve a firearm following an altercation with OT J.C. Latham. Ridley’s case is still being adjudicated, while Elliott landed another tryout opportunity with the Chicago Bears. The Titans released a boilerplate statement wishing Harrell and his family well after the accident, but revealed nothing before the seriousness of the allegations emerged. Now that the allegations are public, the league office and the franchise must do their due diligence. The Titans pass rusher has imperiled his career if these are ultimately proven true. This is the first known off-field incident that Harrell has been involved in since he entered the NFL as a seventh-round selection in the 2024 draft. Harrell landed on injured reserve during the 2026 preseason with an ACL injury, ending his season before it began. In two seasons, he has produced 38 tackles, seven tackles for loss, and 4.5 sacks as a key reserve for the Titans. He was expected to contribute meaningful reps as a backup in 2026, but the injury made it impossible. The allegations are serious enough to warrant a further look by the franchise and league, as the Titans pass rusher involved himself to a degree that a second car was part of the incident. He allegedly assaulted the driver from the backseat, which caused the original vehicle to hit a second one and resulted in damage to a light pole in the end. As a result of the accident, Harrell was thrown forward against the windshield with enough force to require hospitalization. If he is found guilty of what is alleged, jail time is certainly on the table. Financially, the Titans would take a dead cap hit of $ 1,190,000 if he is released during the 2027 offseason, with cap savings of $20,184. It isn’t a huge number that could affect signings in the near future, but a mere rounding error on the cap sheet. As a former seventh-round selection still on his rookie contract, Harrell’s contract is a pittance to absorb easily. More than likely, he will get suspended and/or cut once the authorities, league, and the franchise complete the investigation. The Titans pass rusher involved in the accident could see his aspiring career end before it really could ascend into meaningful reps, due to his own doing. Harre

Mayfield has had a rough start to the 2026 campaign with more interceptions (four) than passing touchdowns (three). However, he's still a better option under center than undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels, who took first-team reps in practice Wednesday for the Buccaneers. Daniels, who has already started three games this season due to injury issues for Mayfield, has also thrown for more interceptions (five) than touchdowns (three). Tampa Bay subsequently has not been very proficient through the air this season. In fact, Todd Bowles’ squad ranks league worst in several passing categories: attempts (240), yards (1,277) and touchdowns (six). Meanwhile, on defense, Winfield is one of the Buccaneers’ very best players. A two-time Pro Bowler and one-time All-Pro, the longtime Tampa Bay defender has been especially stout against the run in 2026. The 2020 second-round pick has earned an 85.5 Pro Football Focus grade for his efforts against the run, the 13th-best run-defense mark among 100 qualified safeties. Additionally, he hasn't been too shabby against the pass, and has allowed just five receptions all season. And for his efforts in coverage, he's earned a 67.7 grade from PFF, the 24th-best pass-coverage mark among all qualified safeties. Consequently, the Buccaneers, which stand at just 3-6, would hardly be in an optimal situation playing without both Winfield and Mayfield on Sunday. As for the Lions, they will be down two of their defensive captains and very best players in Week 11: LB Jack Campbell (neck) and EDGE Aidan Hutchinson (ACL). Hutchinson has already been ruled out for the rest of the season, while Campbell is highly unlikely to suit up again in 2026. Detroit, however, is getting back its All-Pro safety for its tilt with Tampa Bay: Kerby Joseph. Joseph – who was activated off the physically unable to perform list Wednesday – hasn't played a single snap since Week 6 of the 2025 season due to a lingering knee issue. Per Lions head man Dan Campbell, Joseph will be on a “pitch count” Sunday, but is still expected to log more snaps than fellow safety Brian Branch did when he returned from his Achilles’ tear earlier this season. Branch played 45 total defensive snaps in his season debut in Week 7 against the Green Bay Packers. Prior to Joseph's chronic knee ailment , he was a ball-hawk safety. In 55 career games, he's secured 20 interceptions, including a league-high nine during his All-Pro campaign in 2024. If he can come even remotely close to replicating that level of production, he'll provide a big boost to the back-end of the Lions’ defense. At this present juncture, I'll give Detroit a 76 percent chance to capture the Week 11 victory. They're well-rested off their bye week, but they're set to face off against a strong 7-2 Detroit Lions team on the road in what could be the toughest remaining game on the schedule. The Bucs themselves are 3-6, but despite that, they remain one game back from the NFC South lead. The defense has been elite and the run game has been stout, but the passing offense has been a big problem for Tampa Bay — and it may not get much better, as quarterback Baker Mayfield is set to play this game while dealing with a painful plantar fascia injury. As always, we've rounded up our staff to lock in our picks for Sunday's game. Can the Bucs pull off the upset? Or will they fall to 3-7? Caleb Skinner, Writer: Lions 20, Bucs 17 It's getting to the point for the Bucs that they must win, or their season could be over. And things don't get easier this week as they take on the Lions. The Lions own one of the NFL's elite offenses and will test the Bucs' top-rated defense. It's unlikely they'll replicate their turnover margin as they did against the Bears, but they can most definitely slow Detroit down. While the defense won't be too much of a worry, the problems will once again come on the offensive side of the ball for Tampa Bay. The Lions' defense has stepped it up in recent weeks, and even without Aidan Hutchinson, they should be able to stymie the offense enough. I expect this one to be a low-scoring affair at Ford Field, with the Lions coming away with a close home victory to drop the Bucs to 3-7 on the year. Overall Record: 5-4 James Hill, Writer: Lions 24, Bucs 17 Baker Mayfield is once again on the mend from an injury. Yes, the Lions have injuries of their own with Aiden Hutchinson and Jack Campbell, but I don’t know if a hobbled Baker Mayfield or a healthy Jalon Daniels will be able to get the job done. Overall Record: 4-5 Collin Haalboom, Writer: Lions 27, Bucs 21 As much as I believe that the Buccaneers' defense is for real, I also believe the offense is not. Detroit, on the other hand, has one of the most dynamic offenses in the entire league. Beyond just the litany of weapons he has at his disposal, Jared Goff has been extremely effective playing against Bowles' blitz-heavy defenses over the past several years. For the Bucs to win, they'll need to get pressure with four to avoid sending extra guys to disrupt Goff in the pocket. The problem is, even if they do that and manage to generate turnovers like they have been so far this year on defense, the Bucs will need Baker Mayfield to look like a competent NFL QB on offense to win this football game. Sadly, I'm not sure if that version of Mayfield even exists anymore. Overall Record: 6-3 Logan Robinson, Founder: Lions 27, Bucs 20 Another battle for Todd Bowles against a high-scoring offense in Detroit. I’m excited to watch that, but the next thing I’m most intrigued about is the Bucs’ offensive passing attack. That has to improve, or Tampa Bay isn’t making the playoffs — It’s quite simple for me on that. Hopefully the bye week helped, but I’m very cautious about picking the Buccaneers. River Wells, Editor: Lions 24, Bucs 16 The Bucs have a few things going for them, but this is a passing league, and unfortunately, they don't have the passing offense to hang with good teams — much less an elite one like the Lions. The defense will likely hold the Detroit Lions' dynamic offense in check, but the passing offense won't be enough, and it could be even worse than usual with Mayfield's injury. I think the Bucs defense will keep them in it, but it won't be enough to win against a team that could end up winning the brutal NFC North this season. Consensus: Lions 5, Bucs 0 Once again, our staff isn't picking Tampa Bay whatsoever. Our staff unanimously picked the Bears two weeks ago, and we've unanimously picked the Lions here. It's any given Sunday in the NFL, so the Bucs are always in it. But they'll have to convince us that they can beat good teams, and so far, they simply haven't. picks.blurb: Roundtable: Lions Week 11 Preview Against Buccaneers Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Detroit Lions OnSI staff previews the Detroit Lions Week 11 matchup with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. 1. How much is Aidan Hutchinson to blame for his ACL injury? Christian Booher: I think Hutchinson is definitely deserving of some blame for the fact that the injury occurred in such an unnecessary fashion. The movements that went into that injury have been analyzed, and it's rightfully pointed out that a move like the one he did to celebrate that sack poses a risk. However, it's such a fluke situation that it's hard to be extremely mad at the circumstances. He's done that celebration many times, and it just so happens that he has to learn of the risks this way. Vito Chirco: At the end of the day, it was a freak accident and could've happened to any one of the hundreds of players that celebrate after sacks and other big plays. However, as a defensive captain and veteran player now, he should've known better than to leave his feet to celebrate, especially after his previous season-ending injury just two years ago. Consequently, I believe it's fair to say that Hutchinson deserves to shoulder a fair portion of the blame for the ACL ailment. Emmett Matasovsky: It was not the smartest play by Aidan Hutchinson in that injury, I cannot lie. That said, the amount of negative comments towards the EDGE is a bit extreme this week. When a play like that happens, most players’ ligaments tend to be a few plays from giving during game action, frankly. It was not a smart celebration, especially with previous comments to stop the celebrations that could cause non-contact injuries. I will say it is a 60 percent Hutchinson fault, 40 percent circumstance of being close to a natural injury anyway. 2. Are Buccaneers going to be able to slow down Jahmyr Gibbs? Booher : I think the Lions will find some tough sledding on the ground throughout Sunday's game. The Buccaneers have had success against the Lions in past matchups when it comes to slowing down the run game, and with Vita Vea leading the charge, I think the Lions will once again struggle to run the ball. As a result, I think the key to victory is the right arm of Jared Goff, as he'll need to keep the offense on schedule through the air. Chirco : Despite the Buccaneers’ prowess against the run this season, I believe that Gibbs still ends up with a solid day on the ground. And you know that Drew Petzing will also deploy the dual-threat runner as often as possible as a receiver. I expect Gibbs to be contained a bit, but to still produce a couple of big runs in the Week 11 contest. Matasovsky : With the Buccaneers battered and the Lions with momentum, the best hope for Tampa Bay is that Gibbs has jetlag. I think it will be tough sledding for the Tampa defensive line. Gibbs has hit his stride and is coming off a performance of over 250 yards from scrimmage. The fatigue, especially post-international travel, might lead to more Vaki touches, but I do not see the Bucs stopping the Lions running backs room. 3. Who will be Detroit Lions game MVP? Booher : I think Goff is the MVP on Sunday. As I mentioned, the Lions could really struggle to run the ball, which puts more pressure on Goff and offensive coordinator Drew Petzing to dial up counters. Another player that I think is due for a big day is tight end Sam LaPorta, who will likely match up with former Detroit defensive standout Alex Anzalone throughout Sunday's game. Chirco : I'm going to go with Alim McNeill. The run-stuffing interior lineman has had an ultra productive campaign thus far this season, and he will need to come up big Sunday against Tampa Bay RB Bucky Irving. He also will be counted upon even more now as a pass-rusher due to the season-ending injury to EDGE Aidan Hutchinson. With all this said, I believe he'll deliver a solid performance against the Buccaneers, keying a sixth straight victory for Detroit. Matasovsky : It would be foolish to not select Gibbs here. Jahmyr Gibbs has a chance to run free and make plays, especially if Yaya Diaby is out. The back will have a phenomenal backing up from his Munich game, with another effort over 100 yards rushing and two total touchdowns. 4. Will Kerby Joseph make a big impact this week? Booher : I'm tempering my expectations for Joseph in his first game of the season. More than anything, I want to see him be pain-free in his return to action. Before he was officially shut down last year, he would often depart games for a series at a time while dealing with this nagging knee injury, and so I want to see him get through the matchup without having to depart due to pain. Chirco : I'm going to say no. I think the All-Pro safety will log 45-50 total defensive snaps in his season debut. But ultimately, I believe he'll show signs of being hampered by his lingering knee issue. I'd temper my expectations from Joseph in this Week 11 matchup. Matasovsky : I can see this going both ways. I could see Kerby Joseph making a huge play, especially against potentially an undrafted rookie quarterback. However, I can also argue that I see Joseph on a “pitch count” and limited reps. Personally, I hope that it is the former, where Joseph announces he is back with an interception and gets his moment to celebrate in front of the home crowd. 5. What do you want to see from DE Ahmed Hassanein in his debut this season? Booher : Hassanein is a player that is easy to root for due to his mentality and his journey to the NFL. It's been a tough road since he was drafted by Detroit last year, but Sunday will be his first chance to prove he belongs. In the big end role that he will likely play, Hassanein needs to be firm in setting the edge, and I think he could also make an impact with a few pressures if he gets opportunities in passing downs. Chirco : I believe it's reasonable to expect Hassanein to garner a couple of QB hits and pressures in his NFL debut on Sunday. He faces a difficult task going up against the slippery Baker Mayfield. However, the Lions will be counting on the Boise State product to make life at least a little bit difficult for the veteran passer. Matasovsky : Hassanein will have a chance to make an impact, but I will settle for the Boise State product at least making a mark on the box score. It is tough to argue that he deserves more reps than a red hot Derrick Moore, who has four sacks in the last two outings. The former Lions sixth-round pick has earned the right to play, and was likely going to get a chance before Hutchinson’s injury prompted the move up the depth chart. That said, now is the time for the Egyptian. I want to see the player do his job and make positive plays, even if it is not a box score-stuffing day. At the end of the day, the second-year pro is a role player, and football is a game where all 11 players doing their job and role means a successful day. Simply put, I want a penalty free, “plus” day from Hassanein. Published 5 hours ago VITO CHIRCO Vito has covered the NFL and the Detroit Lions for the past five years. Has extensive reporting history of college athletics, the Detroit Tigers and Detroit Mercy Athletics. Chirco's work include NFL columns, analyzing potential Detroit Lions prospects coming out of college, NFL draft coverage and analysis of events occurring in the NFL. Pictured: Baker Mayfield, Jared Goff. Starting soon Odds Updating Soon Matchup - 11/22 6:00pm UTC The Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6) take on the Detroit Lions (7-2) today NFL Week 11. Kickoff is scheduled for 1:00 p.m. ET from Ford Field in Detroit, Mich. The game will broadcast live on FOX. The Lions are 3.5-point favorites on the spread, with the over/under set at 48.5. Detroit is a -210 moneyline favorite to win outright, while Tampa Bay is a +176 underdog. Let's get into my Buccaneers vs Lions prediction for Sunday, November 22. Buccaneers vs Lions Odds Buccaneers Odds 48.5 -110o / -110u Buccaneers vs Lions Spread : Bucs +3.5, Lions -3.5 Buccaneers vs Lions Total : 48.5 Buccaneers vs Lions Moneyline : Bucs +176, Lions -210 Buccaneers vs Lions NFL Week 11 Preview Buccaneers Betting Preview: Mayfield Dealing With Injury Baker Mayfield 's status is in question for this game reportedly due to plantar fasciitis, which could force Jalon Daniels back under center for the Buccaneers . While the market immediately downgraded Tampa Bay, I honestly don't think the drop-off is that drastic in the event Mayfield can't play. Let's look at the underlying metrics for 35 quarterbacks with at least 100 plays this year (removing garbage time). Mayfield ranks 35th — dead last! — in Adjusted EPA per play; Daniels ranks 30th. In terms of success rate, Mayfield is again 35th (32%), while Daniels is 26th (43%). In Completion Percentage Over Expectation (CPOE), Mayfield is 32nd and Daniels is 26th. Mayfield has been atrocious by almost every advanced metric. The biggest difference is air yards ; Mayfield is 8th in air yards while Daniels is 35th. Mayfield has been forcing the ball downfield but is just 4-for-19 on deep passes. Against a Detroit defense that plays a heavy amount of man coverage, Daniels' ability to use his legs would be a huge asset. Expect Tampa to run the ball a ton with Bucky Irving , keeping the clock moving and leaning on a defense that currently ranks No. 1 in DVOA (adjusted for schedule). Lions Betting Preview: Hutchinson a Crushing Loss The Lions defense looks improved over the last month, but context is everything. Look at who they played: Minnesota with Kyler Murray , Miami when Malik Willis hurt his groin and couldn't move, and the Patriots with Tommy DeVito after Drake Maye got hurt. Now the Lions are dealing with devastating injuries that fundamentally change their defensive front. Notably, they lost Aidan Hutchinson , who boasted 52 pressures (second only to Greg Rousseau ) and the highest pass-rush win rate in the league, for the season. Without Hutchinson commanding double teams, everyone else's job gets harder. We will see more of Derrick Moore, who has almost double the missed tackle rate of Hutchinson and struggles to set the edge against the run. The Lions are also missing linebacker Jack Campbell, who was the highest-graded run defender among all linebackers last year, per PFF, and he had a 0% missed tackle rate on run plays this season. When you are missing your best edge player and your best run-stopping linebackers, what do you think the Buccaneers are going to do? They are going to run the football right at you. Detroit is also dealing with questions surrounding its best corner (DJ Reed), and with the Bears on deck on Thanksgiving, Dan Campbell might err on the side of caution with snap counts for guys like Kerby Joseph. Buccaneers vs Lions NFL Spread Prediction The lookahead line was 3.5, and it has leaked all the way out to a full 7 points because of the Baker Mayfield injury news. I was able to grab Bucs +7, but the line has since shifted back to around +4. As the metrics show, the Buccaneers potentially going from Mayfield to Jalon Daniels at quarterback is arguably a lateral move in terms of offensive efficiency. Daniels' mobility actually matches up well against a Lions defense that wants to play man coverage. Detroit is missing its best run defenders in Jack Campbell and Aidan Hutchinson, which should allow the Buccaneers to implement a run-heavy game plan to shorten the game. Tampa Bay has an elite defense that can keep them in this contest, making this line much too rich. away.headline: Buccaneers make Baker Mayfield decision for Lions clash amid injury concerns
away.blurb: Having Mayfield available for Sunday’s game is big, since it involves a hot Lions team that has won five straight games. One has to wonder if he’ll be limited by his injury. Based on the indication that he’s “fighting” through this, it could be something worth monitoring as the two teams face off. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers are heading into Detroit for a battle with the NFC North’s Lions, and Baker Mayfield will be their starting quarterback, despite his recent injury. According to ESPN and NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport , Mayfield is going to fight through the foot injury he has. Mayfield wore a walking boot for several days as part of his injury recovery and reportedly worked “around the clock” to rehab during his team’s bye week. The decision comes as the Buccaneers continue to fight to regain their season. They’re currently 3-6 and nearly upset the Bears in Chicago, but fell 27-24 in the “Sunday Night Football” matchup. Mayfield completed 18 of 32 passes for 242 yards and threw two interceptions in the game. Mayfield suffered the injury, described by NFL insider Tom Pelissero as a plantar fascia foot injury, during that loss on Nov. 8, and reportedly needed new cleats along with a special orthotic. On Sunday, Rapoport explained that the injury is a strain that affects his fascia, a challenging injury for quarterbacks to deal with. More news: NFL Fans Question Nico Collins Fine After Texans’ Loss to Browns According to NFL.com , head coach Todd Bowles indicated that Mayfield was “trending in the right direction” after Friday’s practice. Mayfield was also optimistic about playing when asked on Thursday. “Doing everything I can to get all the treatment and rehab possible and prepare like a professional,” he told reporters. “So, for me … if I continue that, I imagine being able to play.” Mayfield has also dealt with a dislocated right thumb earlier this season. Thankfully for Mayfield and the Bucs, it wasn’t a major injury, but he still missed time, requiring rookie backup Jalon Daniels to start several games. This season, Tampa Bay’s veteran quarterback has thrown for 922 yards and three touchdowns, but also four interceptions in six games. He’s also posted a 2-4 record in those six appearances, as the team has struggled to win. At 3-6, the Buccaneers still have a good chance to turn things around and fight for a winning record. After they face the Lions on Sunday, they’ll host the Carolina Panthers and Los Angeles Chargers. home.headline: Report: Lions' Hutchinson out for season with ACL injury
home.blurb: "Nothing new," Lions coach Dan Campbell said after the game when asked for an update on Hutchinson. "We’ll know more when we get back to the States. But any time you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate he is — he’s a captain of ours — that doesn’t make things easy. But I thought guys stepped up in his wake and showed up for us today and helped us out." This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Report: Lions' Hutchinson out for season with ACL injury Initial tests on Aidan Hutchinson’s injured knee showed the Detroit Lions star has a torn ACL, according to a report from NFL Network on Monday, Nov. 16. Hutchinson, 26, had initial tests performed in Germany, where the Lions beat the New England Patriots on Sunday, and will have more done in the United States, the report added. On Good Morning Football, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said, “my understanding, the belief is it’s a torn ACL and more for Aidan Hutchinson.” The injury to Hutchinson occurred in the first quarter of Detroit’s win over the Patriots. Hutchinson sacked quarterback Drake Maye and leapt into the air to celebrate. He fell to the ground after landing and grabbed his right knee. Hutchinson, who has six sacks this season, eventually walked off the field under his own power. He entered the blue medical tent on the sideline and remained there for a few moments before later walking to the locker room with trainers at his side. Campbell is scheduled to hold a news conference on Tuesday. If the report from NFL Network is correct and Hutchinson does have a torn ACL, D.J. Wonnum and rookie Derrick Moore would be expected to see an uptick in responsibilities. Wonnum has six sacks this season, and Moore has four over his last two games.

Will that trend continue in Week 11? Visiting head coach Andy Reid's crew are Mike LaFleur and the Arizona Cardinals, who managed to capture two wins in three games earlier this campaign but have since dropped back-to-back outings. Down to their fourth quarterback of the year, their work is cut out for them against a surging Kansas City squad. With kickoff on the horizon, which side will come out on top today? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 11 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: In each of the last two weeks, I’ve been able to genuinely argue that the Jets and Falcons were better (or at least more dangerous) than their meager records would indicate. The 3-7 Cardinals are probably worse than their record, especially while they’re preparing to be quarterbacked by a new-in-town 40-year-old super-journeyman. There are no excuses for the Chiefs to stumble in this game. The Chiefs have put up 35 points in each of their last two wins while holding the Jets and Falcons to 12 and 13 points, respectively. With the Buffalo Bills on the horizon, I expect a similarly stout defensive performance, but I wouldn’t be surprised if the Chiefs are content to park the bus offensively if they hold a second-half lead over Arizona. Jordan Foote: Given their recent shellackings of the New York Jets and Atlanta Falcons, it's hard not to think the Chiefs will emerge with a comfortable Week 11 victory over the Cardinals here. Arizona is simply too devoid of talent on either side of the ball, leaving only a bizarre outcome that borders on a miracle being the club's main path to a win. Kansas City's banged-up roster is still miles ahead of Arizona's, with the duo of Patrick Mahomes and Emmett Johnson alone being enough to move the chains. On the other side of the ball, Josh Johnson is an experienced vet, but Steve Spagnuolo may have something in store for him. Give me the Chiefs to roll to 8-2 on the year as the toughest part of their schedule approaches. Joshua Schulman: There’s very little meaningful analysis to provide against an opponent of this caliber. The Cardinals are down several key starters and have been one of the NFL's worst teams over the past handful of weeks. With 40-year-old journeyman Josh Johnson set to fill in for the injured Carson Beck, I’m expecting the Chiefs to steamroll Arizona. Look for Emmett Johnson to have another big game as Kenneth Walker misses his second consecutive game . Tyler Brown: For the third straight week, I think the Chiefs win by three touchdowns. Emmett Johnson could be in line for another career day, and the only thing that may hold him back is a big lead that gets Jadyn Ott into the game. Arizona is ranked 28th in rushing defense. With the offensive line being tinkered with , I expect Patrick Mahomes to experiment with his receiving corps as well. It will be interesting to see whether Josh Downs and Cyrus Allen get a large uptick in snaps, but I am not sure it matters. Any receiver on the depth chart could have a big day against this defense. The Cardinals' offense is as limited as it gets. Trey McBride is their only real weapon, with a wide receiver group where not a single one has topped 100 yards total on the season. Running back Tyler Allgeier is a competent runner but doesn't threaten a defense. Lastly, Josh Johnson, a 19-year veteran journeyman, is under center for a team already on its fourth quarterback. Steve Spagnuolo's key will be limiting McBride, and with the Chiefs' cornerbacks holding down the outside, they should be able to do that. Kelce was not listed on the team’s Week 11 injury report, although they will be without running back Kenneth Walker, guard Trey Smith and tackle Jaylen Moore. Kelce has been productive through nine games this season, recording 35 receptions for 512 yards and two touchdowns. He remains one of Mahomes’ best options and is expected to play a key role in their championship aspirations this season. Philadelphia's other option at quarterback is Tanner McKee, who was terrible. Milton’s mobility does throw a slight wrench into opposing defensive game plans — but he should not be mistaken for a quality NFL quarterback. It's very telling that Pittsburgh got destroyed on national television, the Eagles sat at home on a bye week, and yet the betting market didn't budge this line an inch. The Steelers are a fundamentally sound team that simply ran into the Bengals buzzsaw. But the Steelers match up perfectly against an Eagles team that cannot stop the run. picks.blurb: Steelers vs. Eagles bold predictions for NFL Week 11 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football NFL Week 11 | Latest updates Fantasy Football Toolkit College football winners/losers Current win 1st title Wemby drops 50 ... again Steelers vs. Eagles bold predictions for NFL Week 11 Douglas Fritz, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Tue, November 17, 2026 at 6:24 PM UTC · 5 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Pittsburgh Steelers are hurting in the pride department. Meanwhile, the Philadelphia Eagles are just trying to find their way out of a losing streak. Here are bold predictions as these rivals meet in NFL Week 11. It's weird to write off the Steelers. They have a record of 6-3 and are strongly favored to improve to 7-3 against the weak Eagles. It seems like forever since the Eagles won a game. They beat the Commanders and Titans in tight wins to open the 2026 season before embarking on their current seven-game losing streak. Let's look at what to expect as these teams meet. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers will throw for 225-plus yards with two TDs The Steelers need to re-establish their passing game. They could handle the Eagles by just pounding them on the ground. But this is an opportunity to restore confidence in the passing attack. Rodgers is coming off games with 172 and 143 passing yards. The latter came in an absolute beatdown at the hands of the Bengals. The Steelers need to have good things happen through the air. Rodgers seemed to call out receiver DK Metcalf after the Bengals debacle, according to a post on X by Andrew Fillipponi. "They had a nice plan for some of the run stuff, but they played press coverage, they played a lot of man coverage, and we didn't make them pay at all," Rodgers said after the game. Nobody is going to confuse the 2026 Rodgers with the one who dominated in the past. However, he played well enough for the Steelers to get to 6-2 before the Bengals game. There's reason to believe he can keep this team ahead of the pack when the opponent isn't overwhelming. The Steelers have no chance in the postseason, but they can get there with six more winnable games left on the schedule: Eagles, Texans, Ravens (twice), Panthers, and Titans. Of course, the Steelers will have to make up for the loss of guard Mason McCormick, who suffered a gruesome ankle injury on Sunday night. Head coach Mike McCarthy said there's a plan, according to the Steelers' YouTube page via Yahoo. "Spencer's, you know, he's just a 360 football player, in my view," McCarthy said. "You know, he started out in his right guard and then also the ability to play left guard. He's a gifted football player. This will be his opportunity." Steelers WR DK Metcalf will get 90-plus yards receiving Metcalf has only topped this mark twice this year. He had 115 yards against the Browns and 93 in an overtime game against the Buccaneers. But this is a spot where he could shine again. The Eagles have been middle of the pack against the pass, but they're trending way down overall as a team. There's a good reason for the Steelers to get Metcalf more involved. It not only matters for Rodgers and the team, but the organization has to deal with his five-year, $150 million contract. Oops. If they don't get Metcalf rolling, they may have to look at trying to get out of his contract. That could prove difficult , according to Sports Illustrated. "Cutting or trading Metcalf with a pre-June 1 designation next offseason would make minimal sense, as doing so would incur a dead money hit of $35.775 million while only opening up $2.650 million in cap space for the 2027 campaign (per Over the Cap)," Jack Markowski wrote. "Cutting or trading Metcalf with a post-June 1 designation in 2027 would save $26.5 million against the cap, however, while also forcing the Steelers to take on $11.925 million in dead money." That's just a lot of ugly numbers. Instead, the Steelers are better off trying to feed Metcalf and see if they can restore the roar he had earlier in his career. Eagles QB Joe Milton will throw for 200-plus yards The Eagles need to see what they have in the young quarterback. He completed only 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards against the Giants. But he also rushed nine times for 64 yards. There's something to like about Milton, but he needs to show better accuracy during this audition that could last for the remainder of the season. Milton reviewed his own performance against the Giants, according to philadelphiaeagles.com. "For my first game here, I feel like I did all right," Milton said. "There are a lot of things that I can clean up as far as protection, just helping those guys out with protection. That's something that we're going to get better (at) this week coming up for sure. "I felt blessed, more blessed. That's about it. I felt more blessed than anything. I was able to see my family in the stands, so it was great, but it was also just great to be out there with the guys that I've been here training with for the past three weeks and learning. And just that communication and connection that the team has, and just being a part of it. I love it. It's great. I wouldn't ask for no better situation than this." It won't be easy against the Steelers' tough defense. But look for Milton to battle through for a good game. That's especially true if he can make a big play early. Confidence is an important part of the equation for a young QB. away.blurb: Wide receiver DeVonta Smith is good to go for Sunday's game against the Steelers, but Dontayvion Wicks remains out. The Eagles are healthier coming out of the bye week and will welcome the return of wide receiver DeVonta Smith to the lineup on Sunday against the Pittsburgh Steelers. However, the Eagles will be without Smith's positionmate Dontayvion Wicks for the fourth game in a row. Wicks was limited in practice all week with an ankle injury. The team added a foot injury for Wicks on Friday's report. Linebacker Smael Mondon is doubtful for Sunday's game after missing the past two practices with an ankle injury. Running back Will Shipley did not practice on Friday due to an illness. He is questionable as he remains on Injured Reserve with a foot injury. He would need to be activated off Injured Reserve to the 53-man roster by 4 PM on Saturday to be eligible to play against the Steelers. Linebacker Jihaad Campbell is set to return to the lineup and start alongside Jeremiah Trotter Jr. with Baun out and Mondon doubtful. Campbell missed the past two games with hamstring and quad injuries. Defensive back Michael Carter missed three of the last four games with an abdomen injury. Wide receiver Britain Covey was out for the last two games with a knee injury. Cornerback Jonathan Jones is healthy after missing the past two games with a hamstring injury. The Steelers listed six players as questionable, including outside linebacker Nick Herbig, who suffered injuries to his hip and ribs last Sunday night in Cincinnati. Herbig did not practice all week. Three of the players who are questionable – guard Gennings Dunker, wide receiver Michael Pittman, and wide receiver Roman Wilson – are on Injured Reserve and, like Shipley for the Eagles, would need to be activated in order to play against Philadelphia. Smith told reporters after Wednesday's practice that he was back to 100 percent after missing five of the last six games with a hamstring injury. While the box score and the turnover differential (minus-two) paint a specific picture, the reality is that Baltimore actually played quite well for long stretches of that game against a Chargers team that was playing their absolute "A-game." They were moving the ball well at the end of the half, executing dump-offs effectively, and limiting the disastrous mistakes that Brissett was benched for earlier in the season against Dallas when he was a member of the Cardinals. The biggest takeaway is just how close they were to winning. If Zay Flowers doesn't fumble the football in a crucial spot, Baltimore likely gets at least three — if not seven — points on that drive, which completely changes the complexion of the game. Now, Brissett gets a full week (albeit a short one) to continue building timing with his receivers, which should only improve their offensive output. That is the worst divisional home record through Week 10 in the history of modern NFL divisions. They simply do not possess a true home-field advantage. While the defense might be finding a new schematic rhythm, the offense still has big question marks with Bryce Young slumping after a hot start — asking Carolina to cover the spread as a favorite is a tough ask. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Frank Platko · SB Nation Sun, November 22, 2026 at 3:22 AM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Baltimore Ravens will face the Carolina Panthers on the road in Week 11, looking to snap a five-game losing streak and keep their slim hopes of a late-season turnaround alive. Here are Baltimore Beatdown's predictions for this contest. At this point, it's difficult to pick the Ravens. They are coming off one of their worst losses in franchise history and haven't had life for weeks. Are the Panthers a great team? No, but if the last five weeks are any indication of what Sunday will be like, the Ravens will again be dominated in the trenches, commit costly pre-snap penalties, and turn the ball over in critical moments. The dismissal of Marlon Humphrey could help the team morale, but at this point, Humphrey really isn't moving the needle too much. Simply put, there are too many issues right now. Do I have any confidence that the Ravens will magically be able to run the ball, protect the quarterback, sack the opposing QB, clean up their pre-snap issues, and not the turn the ball over? No. X-Factor: Mike Green. Green has been a bright spot on an otherwise underwhelming defense all year with last Monday being arguably the best performance of his young career. If Green can continue to stack games like that, the Ravens could have a future star on their team. Although Trey Hendrickson has been getting a lot of flak from the media, he's been getting consistently double-teamed and chipped which has allowed Green to take advantage of 1-on-1 pass rush situations. Score Prediction: Panthers 31, Ravens 24 I'm not sure I will pick the Ravens for the rest of the year the way it looks right now. This Panthers matchup might be the easiest remaining on the schedule but with no Nnamdi Madubuike and a drama-filled week with Marlon Humphrey, it just doesn't fill like the Ravens are in a great spot mentally to go on the road and find a win. The Panthers offense loves the middle of the field, something Jesse Minter's defense leaves available by design. Chuba Hubbard has been breaking tackles this season, something the Ravens struggle with. The Ravens offensive line doesn't seem likely to magically improve. If the Ravens win, its because they suddenly learned how to run into sacks against a bad offensive line and because Jacoby Brissett took advantage of an injured Panthers secondary room, that looks to get some guys back this week. I think this is easy win for the Panthers, the Ravens can't stop Hubbard and the Panthers bleed clock for a fast, low-scoring win. X-Factor: Ja'Kobi Lane. Lane was a favorite target in Brissett's debut as a Ravens, who targeted Lane 11 times against the Chargers. Unfortunately, Lane only brought in three of those targets and had a really bad drop in the redzone. He was also tackled multiple times on plays that weren't flagged for defensive pass interference inexplicably. I don't think the Jacoby-to-Ja'Kobi connection is going away despite the low success rate. Brissett loves to push the ball down the field and Lane's skillset fits that well. A breakout game from Lane could drive a Ravens win and maybe flip momentum for the season. Score Prediction: Panthers 24, Ravens 17 The Baltimore Ravens have lost five straight games, with their last win dating back to October 11th against the Atlanta Falcons. This Sunday, Baltimore faces another NFC South opponent in the division-leading Carolina Panthers (4-5). Despite the Ravens' recent struggles and internal drama surrounding Marlon Humphrey, this adversity could be the catalyst for one final push to save their season. The Ravens have a favorable matchup against Carolina's offensive tackles. Rasheed Walker has surrendered 5 sacks and 38 pressures this season, while rookie first-round pick Monroe Freeling has allowed 5 sacks and 26 pressures. Defensively, Carolina has been a buzzsaw against the run, ranking 8th in efficiency and 2nd when stacking the box. However, the Panthers rank just 23rd against intermediate passes, an area Baltimore can exploit. Expect Mark Andrews, Zay Flowers and Ja'Kobi Lane to see a similar target share to last week. X-Factor: Trey Hendrickson: Hendrickson has an opportunity to deliver his signature performance as a Raven. Carolina's struggles at both tackle positions, combined with a tight end room that lacks a reliable option to consistently chip him, create an ideal matchup. Expect Hendrickson to capitalize on these one-on-one opportunities and potentially take over the game as a pass rusher. Score Prediction: Ravens 27, Panthers 16 The Ravens' playoff chances could not be slimmer now after a fifth straight loss last week. However, there is still a mathematical possibility of postseason life — which would pretty much evaporate if they lose any of the next few games. The Panthers are a formidable opponent, but certainly beatable. The Ravens will need to take advantage of Carolina's weak offensive line and create positive plays on defense via the pass rush. Mike Green and Trey Hendrickson have advantageous matchups against both of the Panthers' offensive tackles. X-Factor: Roquan Smith. The Panthers have been one of the top passing attacks over the middle of the field this season, which is Bryce Young's biggest strength. Smith's coverage in this area has been up-and-down, and he will need perform better in this game. The Panthers have multiple big targets who can catch in traffic. Smith will be targeted often and needs to avoid getting lost in open space. Also, can Smith step up as one of the veterans the Ravens need to be more of an impact playmaker? Let's see in this game. Score Prediction: Ravens 21, Panthers 20 It's hard to imagine the Ravens beating anybody after giving the Chargers their first win of the season. This defense holding both Chuba Hubbard and Tetairoa McMillan in check seems like a pipe dream at this point, especially without Nnamdi Madubuike up front. If the offense can finally figure out how to run the ball, then this team will have a legitimate chance, but I will believe they are capable of doing so when I see it. Jacoby Brissett cannot be asked to throw the ball close to 50 times again this week, but with how impossible running the ball has felt at times, he may be asked to shoulder a significant load once again in his second game with the team. That strategy worked out decently well against Los Angeles, but dropping back that many times behind this offensive line is a recipe for disaster over any extended period of time. It is time for Declan Doyle to pull out all the tricks to get Derrick Henry going this Sunday. X-Factor: Travis Jones: Jones had a strong game against the Chargers and the big nose tackle will need to show up again this week for the defense to have a shot at limiting the damage from Hubbard on the ground. Jones will be needed to provide interior pressure as well in the absence of Madubuike. Score Prediction: Panthers 26, Ravens 21
