away.headline: Ravens DT Nnamdi Madubuike misses second practice before Panthers game
away.blurb: Baltimore Ravens defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike missed practice for a second straight day Thursday with a hamstring injury, while rookie right guard Vega Ioane was upgraded to full participation ahead of Sunday’s game against the Carolina Panthers . Madubuike left Monday night’s 23-20 loss to the Los Angeles Chargers and was ruled out in the third quarter. Coach Jesse Minter said Wednesday the Ravens would evaluate how the hamstring responds later in the week. Ioane was listed as limited on Wednesday’s estimated report with knee and shoulder injuries after leaving the Chargers game in the third quarter. His upgrade is an encouraging sign for an offensive line that helped produce just 16 rushing yards Monday. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins remained limited with a knee injury. Running back Adam Randall (neck and hamstring), tight end Matt Hibner (hand) and outside linebacker Mike Green (biceps) were listed as full participants for a second straight day. Carolina tight ends Darren Waller and Tommy Tremble were listed as limited Thursday with knee injuries after both were listed as nonparticipants Wednesday. Running back Chuba Hubbard returned to full participation after a rest day, and outside linebacker Trevis Gipson (ankle) was upgraded from limited to full. Linebacker Bobby Okereke (foot) and safety Isaiah Simmons (knee) remained out of practice. Young (foot) and cornerbacks Will Lee III (hamstring) and Mike Jackson (groin) were listed as full participants for the second straight day. Jackson remains in his return-to-practice window and would need to be activated from injured reserve to play Sunday. The teams’ Friday reports will provide the official game designations. Cornerback Marlon Humphrey was added to Thursday’s report as a nonparticipant for personal reasons. Minter sent Humphrey home Thursday and said the cornerback will be inactive Sunday. The decision came a day after Humphrey apologized for saying on his podcast that Baltimore was “best at making criminals.” Vega Ioane upgraded to full participation Madubuike’s status is the main injury question for Baltimore heading into Friday. His availability will help determine how the Ravens rotate their interior linemen against Carolina and how much pressure they can generate up the middle against Bryce Young. Humphrey’s absence also changes the coverage rotation against a Panthers receiving group led by Tetairoa McMillan. away.blurb: While Jackson has not been officially ruled out for the season, he is expected to be sidelined for an extended period of time, and based on Baltimore's trajectory, it might be too late if and when he does actually return. While a Jackson trade seems incomprehensible, it might not be out of the realm of possibility. The 29-year-old has missed extensive time due to injuries the last two seasons. He sat out four games in 2025, and Baltimore ended up missing the playoffs. This year, he has played in just three contests. Baltimore Ravens Reveal New Update on Lamar Jackson’s Status - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL College football winners/losers Baltimore Ravens Reveal New Update on Lamar Jackson’s Status Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads It certainly has not been an easy year for Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson. Jackson missed three games early on in the 2026 NFL campaign due to an ankle injury. Then, after returning in Week 8, he suffered a thumb injury on the Ravens' first offensive snap, which ultimately resulted in surgery. Ravens quarterbacks coach Israel Woolfork provided an update on Jackson's status Thursday, and unfortunately, he didn't seem to have anything substantial to add. "He's been in and he's focused on his rehab right now," Woolfork told The Athletic's Jeff Zrebiec . What is Lamar Jackson's future with the Baltimore Ravens? The two-time MVP is nearing the climax of a five-year, $260 million deal with the club, one that ends after 2027. There has been speculation that the Ravens could potentially look to trade Jackson before extending him. Given the clear wear-and-tear on Jackson's body, it is fair to wonder if parting ways would be the best thing for both sides this offseason. The Ravens' window seems to be closing, and with Jackson's health deteriorating, Baltimore might be better off starting from scratch. Whether or not it actually happens, of course, remains to be seen. home.blurb: Last week, we talked about the good news of Mike Jackson and Jonathon Brooks fully practicing. It turns out they only took scout team reps and should have been listed as limited participants. Both ended up out for the game against the Saints this past Sunday. Now they are both full participants again, but this time it's for real. Mike Jackson has already said he expects to play this Sunday, which is a huge add for a defense that seems to be turning the corner with new defensive coordinator Todd Wash. He might be joined by rookie Will Lee, who was starting to show flashes before he suffered his own muscle injury. That dup would obviously be a gargantuan upgrade over what the Panthers have had on the outside the last few weeks. No offense. Nnamdi Madubuike – DNP – Hamstring The Ravens' injury report does a disservice to their actual injury woes. Lamar Jackson has had a nightmare season in terms of injuries. He's on injured reserve, and so is backup quarterback Tyler Huntley. The Ravens acquired Jacoby Brissett in an act of desperation, but that hasn't panned out so far. They're relying on newly acquired Cam Jurgens to center the offensive line after they lost several centers to injury over the first few weeks of the season. It turns out he just might not be any good anymore. home.headline: Carolina Panthers vs. Baltimore Ravens: Our predictions, bets, TV, injury report
home.blurb: For Carolina, maintaining its tenuous lead over the horrid NFC South won’t be easy, but it won’t get any easier than facing this struggling Ravens team. And that’s not even a full-throated indictment of Baltimore; it’s mainly a recognition that the Panthers’ schedule, from here on out, is full of difficult games to win. Take a look at their December: at the Vikings, vs. the Saints, vs. the Bengals, at the Steelers. Brutal. What makes this such a winnable game for Carolina (4-5), you ask? The Ravens (4-6) could answer that for you. The team has dropped its last five, including to the previously winless Los Angeles Chargers last week, and hasn’t been able to get future Hall of Fame running back Derrick Henry going; he notched as many carries (10) as rushing yards (10) a week ago, though somehow scrounged out two touchdowns. It doesn’t help that star quarterback Lamar Jackson is hurt, which forced the team to trade for backup quarterback Jacoby Brissett prior to last week’s loss — though, all things considered, Brissett showed that he can still spin it. WRFX The Fox: 99.7 FM. Anish Shroff (play-by-play), Luke Kuechly (analyst), Jake Delhomme (analyst), Jim Szoke (host), Kristen Balboni (sideline reporter). For full local listings, check out the Carolina Panthers Radio Network . Out: LB Bobby Okereke (foot), S Isaiah Simmons (knee), RB Jonathon Brooks (groin), OL Brady Christensen (hamstring) Questionable: CB Mike Jackson (groin), TE Tommy Tremble (knee), TE Darren Waller (knee) Jackson earlier in the week said he’ll be playing on Sunday. As for the tight ends, Canales had this to say to reporters on Friday: “They had a great day yesterday. Didn’t take their full load but took a good amount of reps. Looked good. And came back again today and made more progress. So I’m very hopeful that those guys will be available for us.” Also, Brooks and Christensen were downgraded to “out” on Saturday. Out: S Jaylinn Hawkins (knee), CB Marlon Humphrey (personal), DT Nnamdi Madubuike (hamstring) Alex Zietlow: Panthers 28, Ravens 13. The Panthers haven’t had a stress-free win since Week 2. But one should come Sunday. Some reasons why: the Ravens’ offensive line is forcing Derrick Henry to air out his frustrations to the press. Jacoby Brissett can spin it and is undefeated against the Panthers but is still super new to the system. And most important: The Panthers are due for an explosive offensive showing; I’d be surprised if Tetairoa McMillan is held to under 40 receiving yards for a second consecutive week. The Ravens should be taken seriously nonetheless, what with talents like Zay Flowers in the receiving corps and Kyle Hamilton leading the defense. The Ravens are trying to stay afloat in the playoff race for when Jackson comes back healthy; such hope can lead to desperation — and can spell danger for opponents. home.headline: Carolina Panthers release injury report ahead of Week 11 vs. Baltimore Ravens
home.blurb: As we get set for kickoff on Sunday, the Panthers and Ravens have both released their injury reports for the game. Carolina has ruled out linebacker Bobby Okereke as well as safety Isaiah Simmons for the game. OL Brady Christensen (QUESTIONABLE) TE Darren Waller (QUESTIONABLE) TE Tommy Tremble (QUESTIONABLE) There's some good news as both Waller and Tremble could play on Sunday, giving a boost to the offense. Christensen is also questionable and the Panthers have to make a decision on whether or not to activate him off of IR by Tuesday. Carolina Panthers release injury report ahead of Week 11 vs. Baltimore Ravens PantherRoundtable 175 Members • 1,551 Posts PantherRoundtable PantherRoundtable Related stories REUTERS REUTERS Carolina Panthers Release Injury Report Ahead of Week 11 Zack Pearson Partner Nov 20, 2026 8:29 PM Published Nov 20, 2026 8:29 PM The Carolina Panthers released their injury report ahead of the Week 11 showdown with the Baltimore Ravens. The Carolina Panthers enter Week 11 with a 4-5 record after beating the New Orleans Saints last week . It was a narrow win for the Panthers, but it was an important one. With how tight the NFC South division is, getting divisional wins is key. Doing so on the road is no easy task, and the Panthers proved they could do just that. As they head into Week 11, the Panthers sit atop the NFC South by one game and are looking to extend their lead. They welcome in the Baltimore Ravens , a team that has struggled without Lamar Jackson, turning to Jacoby Brissett via trade. Baltimore is coming off a home loss to the Los Angeles Chargers last week, giving the Chargers their first win of the year. For Baltimore, they are likely not going to catch Cincinnati in the AFC North and the playoffs feel like a long shot if they don't win this game. So yeah, there's a lot on the line for both teams. Here is the injury report for the Panthers: RB Jonathon Brooks (QUESTONABLE) That means that Will Lee, Bryce Young, Feleipe Franks and Trevis Gipson all have no designation and should be ready to play. The two to really keep an eye on are Jackson and Brooks. Both had the 21-day window activated to come off of injured reserve, now it's just when the Panthers do that. They will have to make two roster moves if they do move them to the active roster. But with the struggles in the secondary due to injury, getting Jackson back would be a big win for this defense moving forward. Brooks back would help take some workload off of Chuba Hubbard who has been fantastic the past few weeks. Carolina and Baltimore will kick off at 1 p.m. ET on Sunday.

New York has lost five consecutive games and has failed to cover the spread in its last four contests, including home losses to both the Raiders and the Dolphins . Do not be tempted to take the points in what may seem like a value play — the Jets are deserved underdogs. Los Angeles is in a position we don’t see often in the NFL this late in the season. There have been only 25 games since 2010 in which a team with a winning percentage below 20% is favored in November or during the regular season. When those teams are playing at home, they have covered the number at a 57.9% rate. Technically, the Chargers have won only 11.1% of their games this season. However, it is worth noting that when lowering the aforementioned threshold to teams playing as a home favorite that have won fewer than 12% of their games this late in the season, the results are even better, albeit on a small sample size. There have been only seven such instances, and the favorites have covered in five of those games (71.4%). Understandably, it will feel uncomfortable backing a team that has generally played very poorly compared to the expectations they came into the season with, but that does not mean they are not the right side to back in this game. Jim Harbaugh’s team is still playing hard, and there are signs the second half of their season may play out much differently. The Chargers defense has played admirably given how often the offense has put them behind the eight ball. They grade out as the 12th-best team in tackling, per Pro Football Focus. Their run defense has been particularly stout as they continue to play sound in their gap responsibilities. The Ravens averaged just 1.1 yards per carry against the Chargers on Monday Night Football. For the season’s entirety, Los Angeles boasts the 4th-best defensive success rate versus the rush at 44.3%. For context, that tops the Vikings ' rush defense and is within one percentage point of the Seahawks and Buccaneers — the league’s two premier rush defenses. The Chargers should be able to limit the Jets' rushing attack on early downs and force Geno Smith into obvious passing situations. Smith was erratic a week ago against the Bills , and he left the game multiple times due to injury. Even assuming he is back to full health from an ankle injury that forced him to leave the game in the second half, Smith will face pressure on numerous 3rd downs he will be tasked with converting. The Chargers defense under Chris O’ Leary rarely blitzes, yet it generates quarterback pressure at the league’s 5th-highest rate (38.5%), per Next Gen Stats. Their 17% quick pressure rate, a metric that measures QB pressures that occur within 2.5 seconds of the snap, ranks among the top 10, right in line with other quality pass-rushing units like the Broncos , Packers and Lions . It has to be taken into consideration that the Chargers have not led often this season, meaning they have faced many more rushes than the average defense and have not had the opportunity to rush the passer like they will if they are front-running, like I expect they will against the lowly Jets. Three of the Chargers’ four defensive line starters — Khalil Mack , Akheem Mesidor and Tuli Tuipulotu all rank within the top 25 defenders at their position, per Pro Football Focus. This trio has the ability to win in the trenches against a Jets offense that has been productive only once in the last two months. The full list of players going into Sunday with the "questionable" label are as follows: What Jets Are Saying About Geno Smith and Week 11 Injury Report vs. Chargers Skip to main content SI.COM Another week, another lengthy injury report for the New York Jets. At 2-8, the team is heading to Los Angeles for a Week 11 showdown against the Los Angeles Chargers. The team has dealt with injuries all week to several starters, including quarterback Geno Smith, offensive lineman Dylan Parham, and defensive tackle Harrison Phillips. Whether it's head coach Aaron Glenn or his assistant staff, the Jets believe confident they'll get most of their starters ready to play. Let's break down what the team is saying heading into Week 11. Much has been made whether the Jets should play or sit Smith this week. Some fans wanted him to sit so they would have a better chance of losing. Others want to see their collection of talent on offense look good regardless of the outcome. In the end, Smith doesn't have an injury designation. He will play in Los Angeles on Sunday. "He looks solid," Glenn said. "It's very encouraging." Had Smith not been healthy enough to go, the Jets would have to turn to fourth-round rookie Cade Klubnik. The Clemson product completed 55 percent of his passes in his debut, while also throwing an interception, but the team remains high on his potential. "You could immediately feel it's not too big for him, he was very poised, made throws, you saw his athleticism," Jets offensive coordinator Frank Reich said. "I thought he showed himself well." Smith gives New York the best chance to win . With the Jets doing everything in their power to keep Glenn as coach, it remains clear they will be rolling with the veteran for the remainder of the year...so long as he's healthy. When New York took the field in Tennessee to open up the 2026 season, their full collection of weapons appeared to be a group that could make life difficult for opposing defensive coordinators. Garrett Wilson, Adonai Mitchell, Omar Cooper Jr., Mason Taylor, Kenyon Sadiq, Breece Hall, and Braelon Allen are more than enough to put up points no matter who is quarterback. There's just one problem: the entire cohort of weapons has seen just two series together. Cooper suffered an ankle injury on the opening drive of the season and left after the first play in last week's loss to Buffalo. Losing Cooper to another ankle injury is just the latest missed opportunity for the organization. "He's a difference-maker," Reich said. "You could feel it right from the start and it's been a shame he's had the injuries that he's had because I feel his presence on the field, I feel it when we're game planning." away.headline: Report: Raiders TE Brock Bowers avoids major ankle injury
away.blurb: The team initially listed him as questionable to return and he came back in the second quarter with his right ankle heavily taped. He made one catch before returning to the locker room and ultimately being ruled out. Bowers, 23, finished the 21-13 defeat with two receptions for 18 yards. The third-year pro out of Georgia raised his team-leading season totals to 50 catches for 676 yards with six touchdowns. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Monday that Bowers is day-to-day. "It's not as bad as we thought but still a significant injury, so we'll keep monitoring him," Kubiak said. Bowers, a two-time Pro Bowl selection, was hurt while blocking on a running play during the Raiders' opening drive. Multiple players rolled up on the back of his leg as he was making the block. A first-round pick (13th overall) by Las Vegas in 2024, Bowers has accumulated 226 receptions for 2,550 yards and 18 touchdowns in 37 career games (32 starts). He was a first-team All-Pro as a rookie. This story was originally published November 16, 2026 at 10:59 AM . away.headline: Raiders elevate TE Carter Runyon and DT Chris Williams to face Broncos
away.blurb: Runyon's call-up is insurance for Brock Bowers, who is questionable with injuries (ankle and quadriceps) after a limited week of practice . Klint Kubiak has said Bowers could play without practicing, so the Raiders are planning for their star without counting on him. Williams addresses the other sore spot, the interior of a defensive line that will take the field Sunday at least one man short. Tonka Hemingway was ruled out with a stinger after missing all three practices, while Folorunso Fatukasi is questionable (toe injury) despite a full Friday session. Two lines on the Las Vegas Raiders ' final injury report led to the team's last roster moves before Sunday's trip to Denver. The Raiders elevated tight end Carter Runyon and defensive tackle Chris Williams from the practice squad Saturday, shoring up the two spots hit hardest this week. If Bowers sits, Runyon becomes the third tight end behind Michael Mayer and Ian Thomas, who shook off calf and ankle issues to practice fully Friday. The former FCS All-American from Towson got the same call last week against Seattle, playing two offensive snaps and 18 on special teams in his season debut. Saturday's move is his second elevation of 2026, and NFL rules allow a player only three before he must be signed to the active roster. A lingering Bowers injury would put the Raiders on the clock with Runyon sooner than they might like. Chris Williams adds a body to a thin interior The Raiders signed Williams to the practice squad Nov. 10, the same day Tim Keenan III got promoted to the active roster. The 6-foot-2, 298-pound Wagner product has been around the block since going undrafted in 2020, with stops in Indianapolis, Kansas City, Cleveland, Chicago and Atlanta. His best run came with the Bears , where he played 31 games over two seasons and recorded three sacks in 2024 . Cleveland elevated him twice in October before releasing him from its practice squad Oct. 20. Both players will revert to the practice squad after the game. Game-day elevations let a team carry up to 55 players, so the Raiders bought themselves cover for Sunday without cutting anyone from the 53-man roster. away.headline: Is Brock Bowers playing today? Raiders injury report as TE comes in questionable
away.blurb: Is Brock Bowers playing on Sunday? Raiders TE a real game-time decision Brock Bowers is truly a game-time decision for Sunday's matchup against the Broncos in Week 11. He didn't practice for the Raiders to start to week and then was limited on Thursday and Friday as well. That puts him truly living up to the questionable tag that he's been labeled with for this game and we probably won't know his availability until 1.5 hours before kickoff when inactives are released. With the late start, though, fantasy managers should consider the upside if he plays. Last week, Bowers was also still limited with the ankle injury he's still battling, but he played only 11 snaps in that outing. That's important because we've seen that several times. When Bowers is playing at less than 100 percent, the team has shown no issues with limiting his usage and even his time on the field. When that's the case, he's no longer the must-start TE1, but rather more of a touchdown-dependent option. While there is the chance that he could be fully good to go by kickoff and have his normal high workload for the Raiders in this offense, history tells us that Bowers being questionable likely limits his fantasy upside regardless of if he plays or not. The Raiders have one of the best overall tight end rooms in the NFL with Michael Mayer not just being the proverbial backup to Bowers, but also just being on the field often with Bowers being used as a big slot. Mayer is a startable option each week even when Bowers is healthy, and that continues to be the case even more strongly if Bowers is out or limited and playing. In his debut against a similarly dominant defense to the one the Raiders will see with Denver, Mendoza spread the ball around, especially with Vegas really unable to run the ball effectively. While I don't have high hopes for Ashton Jeanty as a runner against the Broncos, the fact that he led the team in receptions and receiving yards (four for 46 yards) last week makes him someone who will likely get a bump with Bowers either limited or out. The Jaguars have answered almost every challenge that has come their way during the Liam Coen era, and this is another chance to meet the high expectations and standards that the Jaguars have created. For the 7-2 Jaguars, they are fighting to secure the AFC South for the second year in a row, as well as fighting for a top seed in a tight AFC playoff race. To beat the Giants, who have exceeded expectations in their first year under John Harbaugh, the Jaguars will need to be at their best. So, how do we see the Jaguars' big test against the Giants playing out? We break it down with this week's bold predictions. Bhayshul Tuten Hits 100 Yards Rushing No running back has hit 100 yards rushing in a game against the Giants this season, though Kyren Williams and Blake Corum did combine for 164 rushing yards against them in Week 2. Otherwise, the Gians have limited running backs from making a major impact, allowing just four rushing scores from the position this season. With that said, I think we see Bhayshul Tuten have a field day, even with his recent injury issues. According to NextGenStats, "Tuten has forced a missed tackle on 33.3% of his carries this season, the third-highest rate among running backs with at least 100 carries, behind only Kenneth Walker III (38.0%) and Jahmyr Gibbs (36.7%). He has forced 49 missed tackles on the ground, the fourth-most in the NFL, with 267 of his 609 rushing yards coming after forcing missed tackles (43.8%), the highest share among that same group of backs. Giants' defenders have missed 15.0% of their tackle opportunities this season, the second-highest rate in the NFL behind only the Broncos (17.5%)." Add in Tuten's skill-set against a Giants defense that is not great in terms of making one-on-one tackles, and this suggests it could be a good day for Tuten. But the real reason I have him going over 100 yards is bcause I expect him to get at least 25 carries. The Jaguars' entire offensive identity is being balanced, and running Tuten in heavier packages could be the only way for the Jaguars to get the Giants out of their blitz looks. Jaguars Limit Giants to Under 3.5 YPC The Giants have had something going with their running game lately, with Giants running back/mascot Cam Skattebo turning in his two best games of the season over his last two performances. In Weeks 7 and 10 combined, Skattebo rushed 35 times for 202 yards (5.77 yards per carry) for three touchdowns. He has a limited skill-set, but he has been able to pave the way for the Giants running game. With that in mind, I think we see the Jaguars get back to their elite run defense this week after back-to-back weeks allowing too many chunk yards. I think the difference in talent level between Jordan Davis and the rest of the Jaguars' nose tackle options is significant enough that the addition of Davis to the defensive line this week should make all of the difference. The run defense has not been the same without Davon Hamilton, but now the Jaguars finally have their reinforcement set to debut. Parker Washington Makes Another 50+ Yard Catch No receiver has made bigger plays for the Jaguars this year than Parker Washington, who has been the Jaguars' primary downfield receiver all season. He has caught a 50-yard pass in back-to-back weeks, first for a touchdown in Week 9 and then last week to set up a scoring drive against the Titans. With the way the Giants like to play defense with their cornerbacks, I believe this week could be prime for another big Washington grab. According to NextGen Stats, "Washington has averaged 5.0 yards per route against press coverage this season, the most in the NFL, ahead of Jaxon Smith-Njigba (4.7), Mike Evans (4.6) and Tee Higgins (4.4) among receivers with at least 25 routes against press coverage. Washington has faced press on a team-high 46 routes, drawing 16 targets on those plays (34.8%), the eighth-highest target rate among that same group. He has turned those targets into 229 yards (7th-most) and three touchdowns (T-5th-most), while recording 100 receiving yards over expected, the second-most, trailing only Smith-Njigba (+179). The Giants' defense has pressed at least one cornerback on 70.6% of their plays this season, the highest rate in the NFL.." The Giants are going to want to play press-man coverage and challenge the Jaguars receivers at the line of scrimmage. This is where Washington has thrived, and where Trevor Lawrence has trusted him time and time again. I expect another day full of big plays from the Jaguars' No. 1 wide receiver. Jaguars Force 3 J.J. McCarthy Turnovers J.J. McCarthy has not been the turnover prone quarterback that he was in Minnesota in his few games with the Giants, throwing two interceptions over the last month. With that in mind, I think this is the week the Jaguars can let the takeaways flow due to the nature of how McCarthy plays. McCarthy is at his best when he is extending plays with his legs and creating outside of the pocket, but the Jaguars' defense as a whole is meant to counter that. The Jaguars' entire defensive scheme is about forcing the ball out of the quarterback's hands quickly, and these are the scenarios where McCarthy's issues with accuracy and decision-making show up the most. I see the Jaguars getting two interceptions and a forced fumble on McCarthy, largely because the Jaguars' style of defense will let McCarthy play right into their hands. He is playing OK, which is far better than what he showed in Minnesota, but I think the Jaguars get after him this week. Jessie Bates III Plays Every Snap Jessie Bates III did not make his Jaguars debut in Week 10 as they opted to give him the bye week he never got in Atlanta this season, which means Sunday vs. the Giants will be the first time we see the All-Pro safety in Jaguars threads. While the Jaguars took their time with letting Bates and Davis hit the field on game day, I believe their let them play big roles this week. Due to the nature of the position, I believe that means Bates will play every single snap at safety next to Antonio Johnson. The Jaguars have gotten by the last few weeks with Rayuan Lane as their No. 2 safety option, but last week's game against the Titans made it clear that he is better as depth and as a role player. There is no reason for the Jaguars to not let Bates play the entire game this week, which will mark 13 days since he was traded for. away.headline: Jaguars’ Bhayshul Tuten Injury Update Arrives Before Week 11
away.blurb: Tuten was listed on the Jags' injury report for Wednesday as a limited participant. Tuten's limited practice on the first official report of the week is actually a step in the right direction. Jaguars’ Bhayshul Tuten Injury Update Arrives Before Week 11 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL College football winners/losers Jaguars’ Bhayshul Tuten Injury Update Arrives Before Week 11 NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - NOVEMBER 15: Bhayshul Tuten #33 of the Jacksonville Jaguars pitches the ball during the first half of the game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) Getty Billy Heyen · HEAVY Thu, November 19, 2026 at 12:23 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - NOVEMBER 15: Trevor Lawrence #16 of the Jacksonville Jaguars hands the ball off to Bhayshul Tuten #33 of the Jacksonville Jaguars during the second half against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) Bhayshul Tuten didn't have an injury designation last week and got a heavy workload on Sunday, but he evidently isn't 100% of the way past his foot/ankle injury for the Jacksonville Jaguars. Tuten remained on the Jags' injury report that was released Wednesday as they prepare for a Week 11 game on Sunday against the New York Giants. Given Tuten's relative lack of practice time before Jacksonville's last two games, it doesn't immediately appear to be something to worry about, but it's worth noting. GettyNASHVILLE, TENNESSEE – NOVEMBER 15: Trevor Lawrence #16 of the Jacksonville Jaguars hands the ball off to Bhayshul Tuten #33 of the Jacksonville Jaguars during the second half against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium on November 15, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Justin Ford/Getty Images) He remains listed with that foot/ankle injury that he initially sustained in the first quarter of Week 8. Tuten then didn't practice on the short week but played on Thursday Night Football in Week 9. From there, Tuten didn't practice on Wednesday or Thursday in Week 10 before practicing on Friday and playing on Sunday. Considering Tuten had 26 carries for 88 yards and a touchdown in Sunday's win over the Titans, he's probably doing just fine. picks.blurb: 3 Bold Vikings Predictions Before Week 11 SNF vs. 49ers in Mexico City Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI Even if you’re not a fan of the Vikings or 49ers, Sunday night’s primetime match in Mexico City is the definition of a “must-watch.” Two of the best teams in the NFL colliding on the international stage, with playoff seeding and bragging rights on the line, is everything the NFL dreamed of when it set the 2026 schedule last spring. The stakes could not be much higher for a late-November game, and I expect both teams to put on a show. With a newfound Kirk Cousins-sized confidence boost in Minnesota , the Vikings should be set up well to meet the moment. Here are three things I see happening Sunday night at Estadio Banorte. 1. Vikings' defense slows down 49ers' attack The 49ers have been one of the most balanced offenses in the NFL, averaging a league-high 399.8 yards per game. They’re averaging the seventh-most passing yards per game at 255.8 and the third-most rushing yards per game at 144. San Francisco is also second in the league with 31.2 points per game. Simply put, the 49ers' offense can move the ball any way it needs to. The Minnesota Vikings defense ranks 1st in dropback success rate allowed, per @SumerSports The San Francisco 49ers offense ranks 1st in dropback success rate and has the highest dropback success rate of any team through 10 weeks since the 2018 Saints The Vikings' defense, on the other hand, has allowed the fewest points (14) and the second-fewest yards (236.1) per game to opposing offenses. They’ve also held their own against some of the league's best offenses, holding Detroit, Buffalo, and Green Bay to 19, 23, and 10 points over the last few weeks. Now that they have a dependable QB to keep the offense on the field, they’ll be able to catch their breath in the high altitude of Mexico City. Minnesota's defense will need all hands on deck to slow down an elite offense, but Brian Flores will certainly have his unit ready. Give me the Vikings defense to hold the 49ers under 330 total yards and 24 points. 2. Jauan Jennings finds the end zone The Vikings signed Jauan Jennings this past May for two main reasons: to open up the run game as a blocker and to be a reliable third wide receiver after Jalen Nailor’s departure in free agency. So far, neither has materialized the way head coach Kevin O’Connell and interim general manager Rob Brzezinski had hoped. Jennings has also missed the Vikings’ past two games with a calf injury, after previously missing Week 2 to attend to a personal family matter. Now, with Jennings set to return against his former team and WR2 Jordan Addison missing time, the former 49er has his chance to shine . Jennings’s struggles this season have largely been due to poor quarterbacking. The 29-year-old has certainly been open, and Cousins may be the perfect passer to actually get him the ball. I predict that Jennings finds new life and scores at least one touchdown against his former team on Sunday night. 3. Sunday's matchup is only the beginning of what's to come This may already be the NFL’s game of the year. The well-balanced 49ers against the blitz-happy Vikings is a matchup made for the primetime stage. But who says this has to be their only meeting? In fact, if both teams continue on their current paths, a late-round playoff matchup may be an inevitable sequel. You may need to bookmark this one, but I predict that Sunday will not be the last time we see Minnesota and San Francisco battle this year. Whoever takes round two may end up having Valentine’s Day plans at SoFi Stadium. away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, Jordan Addison and Kyler Murray are out as expected, while just Jay Ward and Isaiah Rodgers are listed as questionable. Kevin O’Connell said that Rodgers felt good in Friday’s practice but was limited, and they will see how he feels after practice and with post-practice treatment. More likely both play than not play on Sunday night. For the 49ers, a bunch of players with questionable designations. The biggest two are WR Mike Evans and LB Dre Greenlaw. Evans has been limited all week and listed as questionable, but with Achilles tendonitis I would think they’d want to see how he does with a full speed practice before having him start on Sunday night at altitude. We’ll see. Kyle Shanahan says they’ll see how he does in a Saturday walk-through before deciding on whether he’ll play on Sunday night or not. Dre Greenlaw is dealing with a neck injury and his been limited in the last two practices after missing the first one this week. Kyle Shanahan said that neck/nerve injuries can be difficult to predict, but he’s heading in the right direction. That’s another one that while questionable (which means more likely to play in reality) may be closer to a 50/50 chance. He would be a significant loss if he couldn’t go on Sunday night. Upton Stout is their slot corner and has been limited all week with shoulder/neck injuries and is also questionable. This is reportedly an AC joint issue that he has been playing through since he suffered it early in October so it would seem more likely he continue to play through it on Sunday night, although it has affected his performance. More likely both play than not play on Sunday night. For the 49ers, a bunch of players with questionable designations. The biggest two are WR Mike Evans and LB Dre Greenlaw. Evans has been limited all week and listed as questionable, but with Achilles tendonitis I would think they’d want to see how he does with a full speed practice before having him start on Sunday night at altitude. We’ll see. Kyle Shanahan says they’ll see how he does in a Saturday walk-through before deciding on whether he’ll play on Sunday night or not. Dre Greenlaw is dealing with a neck injury and his been limited in the last two practices after missing the first one this week. Kyle Shanahan said that neck/nerve injuries can be difficult to predict, but he’s heading in the right direction. That’s another one that while questionable (which means more likely to play in reality) may be closer to a 50/50 chance. He would be a significant loss if he couldn’t go on Sunday night. Upton Stout is their slot corner and has been limited all week with shoulder/neck injuries and is also questionable. This is reportedly an AC joint issue that he has been playing through since he suffered it early in October so it would seem more likely he continue to play through it on Sunday night, although it has affected his performance. home.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being 'uncertain' of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, with Kyler Murray and Jordan Addison basically already ruled out, it looks like everyone else is on track to play on Sunday night. However, there was one addition to the injury report- Isaiah Rodgers- who must have injured his quad yesterday in practice and was limited on Thursday. For the 49ers, Mike Evans was upgraded to limited and could be seen jogging through routes in practice on Thursday. My guess is he'll need to be a full participant in practice before they'll play him on Sunday, but we'll see. Other than that, the rest of the 49er's players on the injury report look like they will be on track to play on Sunday night, although I wouldn't be surprised if their cornerbacks were not 100%. Ian Undery Prediction Markets Analyst Download App Updated: Nov 20, 2026, 11:56 AM EST Updated: Nov 20, 2026, 11:56 AM EST 3 min read Credit: USA TODAY Network The Cincinnati Bengals have cleared the 30-point threshold in five consecutive games, a franchise-record streak that underscores the elite offensive firepower orchestrated by Joe Burrow. As they prepare to visit the Washington Commanders this Monday night, one of the most intriguing storylines on the NFL Week 11 slate is whether Cincinnati can maintain this historic pace. Before we break down the matchup and the odds on the board, be sure to use our Polymarket promo code and download the Action Network app to get the best trading insights across sports, politics, and entertainment. Bengals vs. Commanders: Polymarket Odds Cincinnati enters this Monday night matchup as 6.5-point favorites with a 73% implied probability on the moneyline. The consensus total sits at 54.5, meaning traders are effectively projecting a 30.5-point team total for the Bengals. This market has experienced significant line movement over the past week. When Cincinnati secured its fifth consecutive game scoring 30 or more points, their odds spiked. They went from trading at a 64% implied probability on Nov. 14 to their current 73% standing. There are several player props worth monitoring that correlate directly with this 30-point scoring pace. At the top of the board is the performance of quarterback Joe Burrow. His Over/Under totals for completions, passing yards, and interceptions are critical data points. Without another elite showing from Burrow under center, it is highly unlikely the Bengals clear that high-scoring threshold again. The same logic applies to anytime touchdown markets for his primary targets, Ja'Marr Chase and Mike Gesicki, who have already hauled in seven and six receiving touchdowns this season, respectively. New: Can Jaxon Smith-Njigba Break Calvin Johnson’s NFL Receiving Record? Joe Burrow Has the Bengals Offense Operating at an Elite Level Without question, Joe Burrow is the centerpiece of the Bengals' offense. So far, the quarterback has been absolutely lethal, cementing his position as a frontrunner for the regular-season MVP award. Burrow’s elite firepower was on full display in the 38-18 blowout victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers. The quarterback was flawless, completing 35 of 44 passes for 409 yards and four touchdowns without a single interception. With Ja'Marr Chase hauling in 231 receiving yards, the Bengals now look like an unstoppable juggernaut looking to extend its streak this Monday night. While this is the first run of its kind in franchise history, the team is not content with simply writing themselves into the record books. The Bengals have their sights set on a deep playoff run. Is a Taylor Swift tour coming ? Here’s what the odds say. Can the Commanders’ Defense End the Bengals' 30-Point Streak? To stall Cincinnati’s offense, Washington's pass rush must collapse the pocket and disrupt Burrow's timing before he can find Ja'Marr Chase downfield. However, traders remain highly skeptical. The Commanders' defensive backfield has shown a tendency to surrender explosive plays, making them a prime target for the Bengals. To make matters even worse, Washington has already surrendered 30 or more points to multiple opponents this season, including the Cowboys, Colts, and Seahawks. Ultimately, this matchup comes down to pressure versus precision. If Washington fails to generate a relentless pass rush, Burrow will pick their secondary apart, making it highly probable that the Bengals clear the 30-point threshold for a sixth consecutive week. Longest 30-Point Streaks in the NFL and Bengals Schedule While the Bengals have been absolutely lethal, they are still far from the all-time NFL record. That honor belongs to the St. Louis Rams, who hung at least 30 points on the board in 14 consecutive games. Their historic run began late in 1999, the year they won the Super Bowl, and stretched through the first half of the 2000 campaign. Another incredible, and much more recent, streak belongs to the San Francisco 49ers, who reached the 30-point mark in nine straight games across the 2022 and 2023 seasons. If Cincinnati manages to clear the 30-point threshold again against the Commanders, prediction markets’ focus will immediately shift toward projecting this streak down the stretch. As the Bengals navigate the back half of the 2026 season, their remaining strength of schedule presents several tests. The path to keeping this offensive run alive is paved with physical, cold-weather AFC North matchups against the Ravens and Browns, alongside clashes with other conference heavyweights. That culminated in an absolute whooping of the Pittsburgh Steelers at home on Sunday Night Football that wasn't even as close as the 20-point win made it seem. Now they are taking their show on the road to play the Washington Commanders in their house on Monday Night Football. Joe Burrow is 0-2 so far in his career against the Commanders, but that comes with some pretty big caveats. The first loss was the game in which he injured his knee midway through the game as a rookie. The other loss came in an absolute monster of a shootout where the Bengals defense did not stop the Commanders or Jayden Daniels a single time in 2024, with the game ending 38-33. That would not be the first time Burrow would helm a losing team despite putting up more than 30 points over the next few seasons. These teams are drastically different as the Cincinnati defense has had a major overhaul, and Washington is far from the team it was during Daniels' rookie season. There is no doubt Daniels is a talented quarterback, but the Commanders themselves seem to be a very average to below-average team that needs a combination of home run hits on offense and a handful of turnovers to spark a win. Meanwhile, Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins are giving their best impressions of the Colts' offense during Peyton Manning's heyday by trusting their quarterback to put up points with his top weapons over a balanced attack. That has led to four straight games of four touchdowns for Burrow, which ties a record set by Manning. The real x-factor here will be the Bengals defense. Will the version we have seen since the Madrid game against the Atlanta Falcons show up that has been able to contain opposing offenses that tried to test their linebackers and safeties? Or will the young players at those positions allow a few too many big plays? Here is how the oddsmakers and experts feel about the game. The Bengals are currently 6.5-point road favorites against the Commanders, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . It really is a fairly big deal when a road team gets almost a touchdown advantage over a home team. It clearly shows that there is a step between where these two teams are currently at. The point total is set at 53.5 is the second highest of the week. That is fair because even when this team has faced teams like the Tennessee Titans, they have given up opportunities to score. 10 of ESPN's 11 experts are going with the Bengals CBS Sports has all seven experts taking Cincinnati to win All five of NFL.com's experts are expecting the Bengals to extend their win streak to six games NFL Pick Watch — which takes into account picks from across the web — has Cincinnati receiving 99% of the picks for this game. Cincy Jungle Pick I think this team has really turned a corner as far as this defense is concerned. The young linebacker duo of Demetrius Knight and Barrett Carter have grown enough to prove to be a competent — maybe not the most consistent — duo. That is the level of play this defense needs when the defensive line led by Boye Mafe and Dexter Lawrence is able to get penetration. We will have to see how well they contain Daniels, who can really cause some damage by extending plays with his legs. All of that more or less will determine how much the Commanders lose by. Washington has no way of slowing down or throwing off this offense. The Bengals are getting into at least the 30s. Can the Commanders keep pace? Final Score: Bengals 45, Commanders 25 Who Dey! away.headline: Commanders injury updates: Four questionable vs Bengals on Monday
away.blurb: The Washington Commanders got some bad news at the end of Friday’s practice. Starting cornerback Amik Robertson suffered an ankle injury on the last day of practice. He did not practice on Saturday and the Commanders listed him as questionable on the final injury report for Monday night's game against the Cincinnati Bengals . Losing Robertson would be significant. He’s been Washington’s best and most consistent defensive back. His competitiveness sets the tone for the entire team. According to head coach Dan Quinn, Robertson could be a game-time decision on Monday. “So, yeah, [Amik’s injury] on the last play of the day [Friday], so it was sore today, so we held [him] out. I’ll monitor over the next, you know, 48 hours,” Quinn said. In some good news, no players were ruled out for Monday night’s game. However, three others were listed as questionable: Croskey-Merritt had his 21-day window opened last week. Quinn indicated on Saturday that things were trending positively for Washington’s starting running back to return on Monday. White has handled the bulk of running back duties while Croskey-Merritt is out, but Quinn seemed to indicate that he believed White could play against the Bengals. Finally, Patrick is listed as questionable, but practiced fully on Saturday and Quinn said he'd be back in the starting lineup. He suffered a concussion two weeks ago against the Rams and missed last week’s win over the Giants . Former starter Nick Allegretti played well in Patrick’s absence. home.headline: Commanders injury updates: Four questionable vs Bengals on Monday
home.blurb: The Washington Commanders got some bad news at the end of Friday’s practice. Starting cornerback Amik Robertson suffered an ankle injury on the last day of practice. He did not practice on Saturday and the Commanders listed him as questionable on the final injury report for Monday night's game against the Cincinnati Bengals . Losing Robertson would be significant. He’s been Washington’s best and most consistent defensive back. His competitiveness sets the tone for the entire team. According to head coach Dan Quinn, Robertson could be a game-time decision on Monday. “So, yeah, [Amik’s injury] on the last play of the day [Friday], so it was sore today, so we held [him] out. I’ll monitor over the next, you know, 48 hours,” Quinn said. In some good news, no players were ruled out for Monday night’s game. However, three others were listed as questionable: Croskey-Merritt had his 21-day window opened last week. Quinn indicated on Saturday that things were trending positively for Washington’s starting running back to return on Monday. White has handled the bulk of running back duties while Croskey-Merritt is out, but Quinn seemed to indicate that he believed White could play against the Bengals. Finally, Patrick is listed as questionable, but practiced fully on Saturday and Quinn said he'd be back in the starting lineup. He suffered a concussion two weeks ago against the Rams and missed last week’s win over the Giants . Former starter Nick Allegretti played well in Patrick’s absence. home.headline: Bengals Injury Report: Joe Burrow, Dalton Risner on Opening Commanders Injury List
home.blurb: The opening injury report for Commanders Week just dropped from the Bengals . Guard Dalton Risner (knees) did not practice, as fans hope to see him get a session in over the next two days. Joe Burrow was a full participant with his illness so that should quell any fear he may miss Monday's game. Dax Hill is also dealing with an illness. Dylan Fairchild (oblique) logged a limited showing after his injury on Sunday night. Outside of those names, there aren't many big ones to discuss. Cincinnati should get back Andrei Iosivas, Brian Parker and Jalen Davis this week after all three logged full Thursday sessions. Backup safety Kyle Dugger (quad) logged a limited session as a nice sign of improvement. A few other special-team names popped up with illnesses but what looks like a big injury list should end up thinning out across the next few days. "Yeah. Those guys have been so good, and I love playing with them," Burrow said about Drew Sample and Chase Brown. "They take it very seriously, and they want to win. They want to be great, and they put so much mental energy into working throughout the week to understand the guys they're going against. To understand what their pass rush moves are and all the different front looks that we can see. I know that they're not satisfied either, but those guys are lights out." "We've already had all the confidence in the world," Burrow said on Sunday about the team's execution and improvement following a 2-2 start. "This happened on Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday practices, and the rest took care of itself on Sunday. I think we all had a good feeling about what was going to happen today, and we went out and made it happen ... We just kept getting better — just grinding at practice and improving, (and) improving through meetings. We've got great coaches that make adjustments and try to put us in really good positions to go and make plays, and right now we are." Cincinnati has a pretty full arsenal of talent to attack teams with despite the above injuries. Joe Burrow was really excited to feed so many different players for touchdowns against Pittsburgh. Burrow's squad is executing well during practice and should be able to keep that going this week, especially getting an extra day to rest before sparking the session back up today.
